data.title: Trust Me, I'm Local: Chrome Extensions, MCP, and the Sandbox Escape
data.author: el_duderino
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Chrome扩展程序与本地MCP（Model Context Protocol）服务器交互所带来的严重安全风险。MCP服务器通常缺乏身份验证机制，导致任何Chrome扩展可以在无需特殊权限的情况下访问本地资源，甚至可能完全接管机器。文章描述了一个实例：一个Chrome扩展与本地MCP服务器通信，未经认证即可操作文件系统等敏感资源。由于Chrome的沙箱模型无法阻止这种攻击，用户面临极大的安全威胁。文章呼吁开发者和用户重新评估本地MCP服务器的安全性，以防止潜在的灾难性后果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Chrome扩展和MCP（以及更广泛的应用程序）在本地服务器连接和安全方面的潜在风险与解决方案

不同观点：
• telotortium认为，文章提到的问题与MCP没有直接关系，而是Chrome扩展本身可以通过localhost端口进行HTTP连接，只要有服务器运行即可，且扩展已经需要权限才能与localhost通信。
• vovkasm指出，尽管与MCP无关，但操作系统缺乏对本地TCP连接的便捷且可靠的访问控制机制，这导致用户无法方便地控制哪些应用可以连接到特定本地端口，类似问题也存在于其他本地服务器应用程序中。
• fluffet从历史角度出发，认为当前的AI工具忽略了早期互联网协议已经学习到的安全教训，强调需要监管和更稳健的协议设计。
• npace12介绍了自己开发的"little-rat" Chrome扩展，它可以跟踪和阻止其他扩展的流量，以此作为应对措施。
• bhelx建议将MCP服务器运行在沙盒环境中，尤其是使用WASM技术，这样可以提高安全性，并提到可以通过SSE传输数据。
• OsrsNeedsf2P提出，MCP可能因为没有安全摩擦而击败了其他竞争对手，暗示安全性可能不是其成功的关键因素。
• skybrian认为，“允许连接到localhost”的权限过于宽泛，用户很难据此做出明智的安全决策，建议本地服务器应加入认证机制。
• ramoz表示，当前所谓的“新零日AI漏洞”实际上只是暴露了标准安全实践中的老问题，强调本地应用开放连接和没有CORS限制本身就存在风险。
• happyopossum指出，问题与MCP无关，任何监听localhost的应用都可能面临类似风险，扩展只是利用了这些漏洞。
• fpoling建议，本地运行的服务应该拒绝带有Origin头的HTTP请求，以及通常拒绝带有UserAgent的请求，以此作为一种防护手段。
• babyshake询问是否使用streamable HTTP MCP服务器可以避免某些漏洞，并讨论了STDIO/SSE的必要性。
• brap质疑为何需要新的协议（如MCP），认为现有的OpenAPI规范已经足够，且支持广泛的API和认证机制。
• olalonde提出了具体的解决方案问题，询问是通过在MCP服务器上添加认证机制，还是通过Chrome限制未经授权的localhost调用来解决安全问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于MCP是否是问题的核心，还是这只是更广泛的Chrome扩展和本地服务器安全问题的一部分。
• 一些参与者（如vovkasm、skybrian）强调了操作系统或浏览器应提供更好的访问控制机制，而其他人（如ramoz、happyopossum）则认为这并非新问题，只是现有安全风险的延伸。
• 提出了多种技术解决方案，如使用WASM、加入认证机制、拒绝特定HTTP请求等，但尚未达成一致意见。
• 部分讨论也涉及AI工具和协议的设计是否忽视了早期的安全教训，呼吁更稳健的协议和监管措施。

Trust Me, I’m Local: Chrome Extensions, MCP, and the Sandbox Escape
Yuval Ronen
Follow
6 min read
·
Apr 24, 2025
--
Listen
Share
Let’s talk about MCPs. You’ve probably heard of them, and maybe you’ve read the security risks associated with them. Sure, they sound worrying, but when you put them into a real-world context, they can quickly become far more concerning than you can ever imagine.
Just last week, our system flagged a suspicious Chrome extension. It sent messages to a port on localhost — nothing too odd at first glance, but as we dug deeper, we found that this extension communicated with an MCP server running on the local machine.
The fact that Chrome extensions can communicate with MCPs is a serious risk. The consequences are enormous. The usual security measures like Chrome’s sandbox model, don’t stand a chance.
You’re looking at unauthenticated access to the filesystem and, in some cases, a full machine takeover. That’s not just a small issue;
that’s a massive, game-changing vulnerability.
And here’s the kicker:
any
Chrome extension can exploit this. No special permissions required. If there’s a vulnerable MCP server running on a host machine, that’s it. We’ve already found vulnerable MCP servers tied to services like filesystem access, Slack, WhatsApp, and more. This isn’t just a theoretical risk anymore, it’s real, and the impact could be devastating.
So, if you’re running MCP locally, it’s time to seriously reevaluate your security. We were mindblown when we found this, and it’s time everyone else takes notice before it’s too late.
So, buckle up and get ready, let’s dive into this together.
A Suspicious localhost connection
While monitoring browser extension activity, our detection engine flagged a Chrome extension making network requests to localhost. Although the extension itself showed no signs of malicious behavior, the destination caught our attention. It was communicating with a local service implementing the
Model Context Protocol (MCP)
— a protocol used to interface AI agents with system tools and resources on the endpoint.
localhost MCP connection from chrome extension
This raised an immediate concern: if a browser extension can talk to an MCP server running on the user’s machine, what’s stopping it from accessing sensitive resources or executing privileged actions through the MCP?
MCP: Open by Default
Let’s first understand how MCP clients communicate with MCP servers. There are 2 standard transport implementations -
Server-Sent Events (SSE) — enables the MCP server to communicate through HTTP POST requests.
Standard Input/Output (stdio) — enables the MCP server to communicate through the process’s standard input and output streams.
When implementing an MCP server, the developer can choose how the MCP server will communicate. The server can support both transport methods.
It’s important to note that the transport layers themselves do not implement, or require, any authentication mechanism. It is up to the MCP server developer to implement access controls, but in practice, nearly all MCP servers today do not enforce authentication by default.
For local use, an MCP server that relies on Server-Sent Events (SSE) typically binds to a port on localhost, making it accessible from processes running on the same machine (like an MCP client).
Sandbox, Meet Sledgehammer
Now that we understand how a local SSE-based MCP server operates, and that it’s generally accessible to processes running on the same machine, we can revisit the question: can a Chrome extension access it as well?
The communication flow is fairly straightforward:
The client sends a GET request to the server to obtain a session ID and a messages endpoint — without any form of authentication.
Once initialized, the client can issue POST requests to that message’s endpoint to retrieve the list of available tools exposed by the MCP server and invoke them directly.
Client-Server communication illustration
First we set up a local SSE-based MCP server from
mcp.so
, specifically choosing a file-system variant, which allows AI clients to interact with the local file system. Following the setup instructions in the server’s README:
node dist/index.js ~/work/mcp/private_directory
Next we built a Chrome extension that runs in the background and attempts to connect to localhost:3001 - a commonly used port for local SSE-based MCP servers. Of course, this port may vary, so a real-world extension would need to scan local ports to locate the active MCP instance. The extension gets the server information, retrieves the tools list and tries to invoke the tools provided by the MCP server:
The Chrome extension had
unrestricted
access to the MCP server’s tools — no authentication needed — and was interacting with the file system as if it were a core part of the server’s exposed capabilities. The potential impact of this is massive, opening the door for malicious exploitation and complete system compromise.

data.title: Owen Le Blanc: creator of the first Linux distribution
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了Owen Le Blanc及其创建的第一个Linux发行版MCC Interim Linux。1992年初，Le Blanc在曼彻斯特计算中心（MCC）工作时开发了这一发行版，旨在简化Linux的安装过程。当时，Linux内核虽已发布，但缺乏易用的安装工具，Le Blanc利用了Ted Ts'o的ramdisk代码和H. J. Lu的原型发行版，并编写了首个Linux fdisk工具。MCC Interim Linux通过两张软盘安装，显著提高了安装效率，被用于大学课程。虽然最初版本难以找到，但后续版本保存在ibiblio等档案中。该项目持续约七年，最后更新于1998年初。尽管未商业发行，但被包含在一些Linux工具包CD中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux早期历史和不同发行版本的贡献与影响

不同观点：
• spacedcowboy认为自己在1992年为Atari ST/TT系列制作的类Unix发行版是首个此类版本，安装了MiNT以及其他工具，并提供了安装帮助文档。
• fsiefken提供了更多背景信息，提到MCC Interim Linux的早期版本，并分享了相关链接，表达了对编译和优化的兴趣。
• nikdoof回忆了与Linux相关的经历，提到了Manchester Linux User Group和早期与知识渊博的人的连接。
• mprstn回忆了作为Ph.D.学生时被Owen介绍Linux的经历，表达了对Owen贡献的赞赏。
• noufalibrahim感叹历史中的无名英雄，提出了关于“挠痒式”解决方案成为主流后被遗忘的问题。
• dehrmann质疑发行模式对Linux的影响，指出服务器发行版的合理选择和桌面发行版的碎片化问题，并提到了Android和ChromeOS的流行。
• kpw94指出1992年2月的首个Linux发行版和三个月后发布的带有GUI的“TAMU Linux”，均为大学发布。
• TomMasz回忆了90年代早期安装软件的困难，提到曾尝试Yggdrasil CD但未能成功安装。
• stuaxo提到文章评论区中人们对MCC Interim Linux和Owen的回忆。
• dnisbet表达了对与Owen共事的回忆和美好记忆。
• lproven提到之前的相关讨论，未有评论。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到早期Linux发行版的安装困难、技术贡献者的回忆以及Linux发行模式对后来技术发展的影响。
• 争议焦点在于Linux发行模式是否对桌面发行版的碎片化产生了负面影响，以及对无名贡献者的认可问题。
• 讨论还涉及到对具体发行版本和技术细节的历史考证。

Owen Le Blanc: creator of the first Linux distribution
By
Joe Brockmeier
April 21, 2025
Ask a Linux enthusiast who created the Linux kernel, and odds are they will have
no trouble naming Linus Torvalds—but many would be stumped if asked what the
first Linux distribution was, and who created it. Some might guess
Slackware
, or its predecessor,
Softlanding Linux
System
(SLS); both were arguably more influential but arrived just a bit
later. The first honest-to-goodness distribution with a proper installer was
MCC Interim Linux
,
created by Owen Le Blanc, released publicly in early 1992. I recently
reached out to Le Blanc to learn more about his work on the distribution, what
he has been doing since, and his thoughts on Linux in 2025.
When Torvalds first released the Linux kernel, he also provided "boot" and "root"
disk images (intended for
5¼-inch
floppy disks
) to help users
create a Linux system. There was not a proper installer, and users had to collect
several other utilities to pull together a working system. This was not, even for the
time,
particularly
user friendly
. Clearly, Linux was going to need a little extra help on its path
to world domination.
MCC Interim Linux
Le Blanc worked for the Manchester Computing Centre (MCC) at the
University of Manchester
from 1985
through 2016. He had been working with
CDC 7600
and
Cyber 170/730
machines, and
eventually began working with
HP 9000
workstations. Those ran
Hewlett Packard's Unix,
HP-UX
, which
made him want to learn more about Unix. He started with
Xenix
, but wanted something easier to
use. He said that he also tried
MINIX
, but it was difficult to get
working on a
Intel 80486 CPU
. When
Torvalds announced Linux, Le Blanc decided to give it a try, and that too was a
fair amount of work.
It was fairly hard to install Linux at first, because I think you
needed both MS-DOS and Minix -- we used a bootloader from Minix before
Werner Almesberger wrote LILO. You needed Minix because the DOS fdisk
program could not write partitions for other operating systems, and
you needed DOS if you wanted to do networking.
He was interested in improving the installation and created a Linux
system that could be installed from a pair of floppy disks. He made
use of ramdisk code by Ted Ts'o, took binaries from a
proto-distribution
created by H. J. Lu, and he wrote the original Linux fdisk
"
bugs and all
" for the project. According to the
MCC
README
for version 0.99.p10+, Le Blanc used his
distribution to install Linux on
386-SX
machines
for the university's C and Unix courses. It was possible to install
Linux on 12 machines in about an hour, according to the
documentation, certainly an improvement over earlier installation
methods. Eventually, he asked his department if he could share the
work that he had been doing.
The department was reluctantly willing, provided (1) I gave them some
credit for supporting its development, and (2) I made certain they had
no responsibility for ongoing support for users.  We agreed that
calling it "MCC Interim Linux" suggested that MCC had developed it,
and it was not intended to be a long term project.
The first MCC Interim Linux release (0.12) from February 1992, is,
if not completely lost, certainly hard to find online. The
1.0
release
is preserved on the ibiblio archive with other
historic
distributions
such as Yggdrasil, Red Hat's "Mother's Day" 1.0
release, and SLS 1.03 and 1.05.
The distribution
included things like
GCC
,
GNU Awk
,
GNU Emacs
, and the
info
packages because they were used in the university's courses. He did
not attempt to include a wide assortment of other software, such as
XFree86
(then X386), though.
$ sudo subscribe today
Subscribe today and elevate your LWN privileges. You’ll have
access to all of LWN’s high-quality articles as soon as they’re
published, and help support LWN in the process.
Act now
and you can start with a free trial subscription.
Later releases can be found on
debian.mcc.ac.uk
,
in the
non-debian
directory. It has several releases, up to
the final
2.0
release
from 1996. I had asked Le Blanc whether MCC had
been distributed commercially, and he said no one had ever sold copies
of MCC that he was aware of though "
there were certainly people who
passed disks to others
". While doing some digging, though, I found
that
Walnut
Creek
had included MCC in some of its Linux Toolkit CD sets. For
example, the Internet Archive has the
March 1997
set with MCC Interim Linux 1.0+, along with Slackware, Debian,
MkLinux, and others. Readers who have older Linux Toolkit CD sets, or similar
sets, gathering dust in their closets may have even earlier versions.
In all, Le Blanc said that the
project ran about seven years, with the last updates to the
distribution being released in early 1998. Duri

data.title: Anubis saved our websites from a DDoS attack
data.author: DoctorOW
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在ScummVM项目中经历的一次DDoS攻击事件。起初，作者收到服务器负载增加的监控通知，但未发现明显异常。几天后，网站因服务器过载而崩溃，Apache、PHP-FPM和MariaDB均达到饱和。通过检查日志，作者发现大量来自同一IP的可疑请求，试图通过频繁访问特定页面来压垮服务器。最终，作者通过封锁该IP并优化服务器配置成功抵御攻击，网站恢复正常运行。此次事件被戏称为“阿努比斯拯救了我们的网站”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Anubis及其在防止DDoS攻击和AI爬虫方面的有效性与使用讨论

不同观点：
• **mrweasel**：不确定当前的攻击是DDoS还是AI爬虫引发的问题，认为现代AI公司不像传统搜索引擎那样尊重互联网基础设施，隐匿行为更明显，导致难以区分恶意攻击和爬虫行为。
• **CaptainFever**：认为Anubis只是DDoS保护工具的更新版，本质上与已有工具（如CloudFlare等）类似，质疑为何Anubis受到特别关注，可能只是因为营销得当。
• **chrisnight**：指出Anubis的验证机制对使用临时容器插件的用户不友好，每次关闭标签页后都需要重新生成token，尽管理解隐私保护的需求，但体验不佳。
• **butz**：提出Anubis部署后可能带来一些意外问题，例如影响正常文件下载或导致链接失效，强调需要仔细检查其对系统的影响。
• **vachina**：认为任何简单的验证机制（如Captcha或按钮点击）都能有效阻止大多数爬虫，不必依赖Anubis。
• **forty**：建议将PoW（工作量证明）系统集成到HTTP或TLS协议中，以避免对JS的依赖。
• **kh_hk**：指出当前的客户端PoW可能不足以长期应对，爬虫可以通过解决挑战并重用cookie绕过限制，提出使用JA4指纹识别作为额外验证手段。
• **Tiberium**：质疑Anubis对“诚实”标识用户代理的惩罚机制，认为这可能会促使爬虫伪装身份，奖励那些不道德的爬虫行为。
• **justusthane**：不理解Anubis如何解决特定DDoS问题，尤其是当攻击来自僵尸网络时，为何这些机器不花额外时间解决PoW。

补充讨论：
• **qiu3344**：支持Anubis，认为其抗爬虫机制比传统WAF/抗爬虫大厂更有效，且不依赖浏览器特性，避免了浏览器垄断文化的支持问题。
• **pmlnr**：询问是否有不依赖JS的解决方案。
• **gitroom**：提到Anubis涉及到开源社区中的法律规则和个人需求的平衡问题。
• **8474_s**：偏好Anubis的验证方式，认为比Cloudflare的验证更友好。

争议焦点：
• Anubis是否因为营销得当而受到过度关注，其实质是否与其他DDoS保护工具并无显著区别。
• Anubis对“诚实”标识用户代理的惩罚是否会适得其反，导致更不道德的爬虫行为。
• Anubis部署后对系统正常功能的可能影响及如何权衡其副作用。

总结：讨论围绕Anubis的实际效果、其对用户和系统的影响以及是否应该使用不依赖JS的解决方案展开，反映了技术社区对网络安全工具的复杂需求与权衡。

The Day Anubis Saved Our Websites From a DDoS Attack
2025-05-01 14:00:00
#bts
#sysops
#webdev
One part of my work for the ScummVM project is helping to keep the server infrastructure up and running, including our primary server, which hosts our website, wiki, forums, and some internal applications.
About three weeks ago, I started receiving monitoring notifications indicating an increased load on the MariaDB server. This in itself is nothing too unusual. It usually means nothing but a sudden influx of new visitors, and in most cases, it is just a link being shared somewhere or a single IP trying to annoy us.
The notifications popped up and disappeared as quickly as they appeared. I started to look into the log files of our web server, and I didn’t notice anything too unusual, maybe a bit more background noise. This went on for a couple of days without seriously impacting our server or accessibility–it was a tad slower than usual.
And then the website went down.
We use a stack consisting of Apache2, PHP-FPM, and MariaDB to host the web applications. The server logs revealed that everything was saturated. Apache2 refused to accept new connections, the PHP-FPM pools were completely filled, and MariaDB also had no connections left.

data.title: Altair at 50: Remembering the first Personal Computer
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 《Altair at 50: 纪念第一台个人电脑》一文回顾了1975年由MITS公司推出的Altair 8800，这台电脑被认为是首台商用成功的个人电脑，比苹果和Commodore的电脑更早。Altair基于Intel 8080 CPU，通过《Popular Electronics》杂志宣传，以397美元的套件形式出售，用户需自行组装，初期仅有256字节RAM，无键盘和显示器，通过开关和指示灯操作。尽管初期计划售出200套以达到收支平衡，但最终卖出了约25,000套，激发了比尔·盖茨和保罗·艾伦为其开发BASIC语言，进而促成了微软的成立。Altair还启发了史蒂夫·沃兹尼亚克设计第一台苹果电脑，并引入了S-100总线，对后续计算机产生深远影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Altair 8800电脑的历史、影响、及其相关技术细节的讨论。

不同观点：
• **关于Altair 8800的模拟器**：musicale列举了多个Altair 8800的模拟器链接，指出可以在这些模拟器上运行CP/M系统，但也提到其使用上不如其他CP/M模拟器方便。
• **对Ed Roberts的个人生平的关注**：NoSalt对Altair 8800的发明者Ed Roberts的生平做了详细描述，强调了他多重职业背景和成就。
• **对历史杂志内容的兴趣**：shakna被评论中的杂志封面吸引，提到杂志中关于计算器组装的详细步骤，并提供了相关链接。
• **个人经历与历史设备**：embedded_hiker分享了自己在学校期间通过 teletype 和HP2000C学习编程的经历。CarVac提到自己拥有IMSAI 8080设备，并讲述了其教授不建议他从事计算机职业的故事。
• **Altair 8800的价格与复刻版**：danbruc对比了Altair 8800当年的价格和如今在eBay上的售价，并提到现在有售价150美元的迷你复刻版。
• **其他早期计算机的提及**：jodydonetti提到Olivetti P101（1965），oldnetguy则认为Kenbak 1才是第一台个人计算机，dcassett补充了Mark-8这个早期的"套件计算机"。

补充讨论：
• **对微软诞生历史的影响**：igtztorrero强调了Altair 8800对微软创立的重要影响，提到比尔·盖茨和保罗·艾伦如何在Altair 8800上开发BASIC语言，并促成了微软的诞生。
• **个人捐赠经历**：vondur提到自己从岳父那里得到了Altair 8800并捐赠给了当地大学。
• **对早期PC的认知**：berlinbrowndev表示自己原以为TRS和Commodore 64才是最早的个人电脑，显示出对Altair 8800作为早期PC代表的不了解。

争议焦点：
• **最早的个人计算机之争**：在提到Altair 8800时，有人认为它是第一台个人计算机，但oldnetguy提出Kenbak 1更早，而dcassett则补充了Mark-8这个早期的"套件计算机"，显示出对"第一台个人计算机"定义的不同看法。

总结来看，评论主要围绕Altair 8800的历史地位、技术细节、相关模拟器及其对个人计算机历史的影响展开讨论，同时掺杂了一些个人经历和相关早期计算机的提及。

You might think that Apple, Commodore or perhaps Radio Shack made the first personal computer, but you’d be wrong. Although the Apple I appeared in 1976, and then in 1977 the Apple II, Commodore PET and TRS-80 all appeared, there was one personal computer that preceded them all: The MITS Altair 8800 from 1975, considered the first commercially successful personal computer.
The Altair was created by a small company called MITS, which initially stood for Micro Instrumentation and Telemetry. In 1974 MITS had been selling calculator kits via mail order. Later in the year they started working on a computer based on the then-new
Intel 8080 8-bit CPU
. About this time they were contacted by Popular Electronics magazine who was looking to do a feature on a computer project.
The Altair name was taken from the brightest star in the Aquila constellation. It is one of the closest stars to Earth and the name was considered futuristic.
This all coincided with the January 1975 issue of Popular Electronics. The Altair
1
was featured on the cover and there was a companion article (written by Ed Roberts, owner of MITS) titled “Project Breakthrough! World’s First Mini-computer Kit to Rival Commercial Models”.
The computer kit sold for $397 (about $2359 in 2023). Being a kit, that meant that you had to assemble the computer yourself. It didn’t even have a keyboard or display as you used it via its toggle switches and blinking lights!
If you love retro computing, please consider subscribing to Goto 10. Thanks!
Subscribe
For your money you got the case, power supply, motherboard, CPU board, front panel with switches and LEDs, 256 bytes of RAM and assembly instructions. You could pay a little more and have it pre-assembled for you, but that would have delayed delivery. It was so popular that people were known to drive to Albuquerque, New Mexico to personally pick one up!
The Altair doesn’t look all that “personal” today, but it is considered a personal computer because a single person could afford to purchase it themselves, something remarkable for 1975.
Initially MITS had hoped to sell about 200 kits in order to break even, but they sold many, many more than that. Estimates are that about 1,000 were sold in the first month and that about 25,000 kits were sold in total. The percentage of those kits that were successfully assembled by customers is likely pretty low, however. I suspect many people wanted (and bought) one just so they could say they had a computer!
Jan 1975 Popular Electronics

Download
Download
The Popular Science article caught the eyes of Bill Gates and Paul Allen. Bill was a student at Harvard at the time and he knew Paul from when they both attended Lakeside School in Seattle. They decided they needed to jump on this new industry that was forming before their eyes and worked quickly on a version of BASIC for the Altair.
This BASIC was implemented on the Harvard PDP-10 mainframes by Bill and others (using an emulator they also had to write since they didn’t have an actual Altair to use), with Paul Allen flying to Albuquerque New Mexico in the summer to demonstrate it to Ed Roberts.
There were some ethical questions regarding the use of the Harvard computers to development commercial software. I believe Harvard put some rules in place to prevent this from happening again.
A deal was made and Microsoft (or Micro Soft as it was at the beginning) was formed. BASIC gave the Altair an actual useful program and made it easier for people to write their own programs, although you needed to also upgrade the Altair to at least 4K of RAM ($$$) to even run it.
On April 2 2025, the 50th anniversary of Altair BASIC,
Bill Gates made the original assembly source code available in the form of a PDF
. Others have since put it on
GitHub in text format
.
A snippet of the Altair BASIC assembly source code
The Altair didn’t survive for very long, but essentially being responsible for the creation of Microsoft is a pretty Big Deal. It also inspired a young Steve Wozniak to create the first Apple computer, using the less expensive MOS 6502 CPU. This first Apple I was also primarily a kit.
The Altair also introduced the S-100 bus that became a standard that was used in a variety of other niche computers around the late 70s.
I was able to see an Altair 8800 when I visited the London Science Museum a couple years ago. It was somewhat larger than I expected.
Altair 8800b computer with a photo of Ed Roberts and the January 1975 issue of Popular Science that kicked off the personal computer industry.
Here is the text from the placard:
Altair 8800b personal co

• **对Ed Roberts的个人生平的关注**：NoSalt对Altair 8800的发明者Ed Roberts的生平做了详细描述，强调了他多重职业背景和成就。
• **对历史杂志内容的兴趣**：shakna被评论中的杂志封面吸引，提到杂志中关于计算器组装的详细步骤，并提供了相关链接。
• **个人经历与历史设备**：embedded_hiker分享了自己在学校期间通过 teletype 和HP2000C学习编程的经历。CarVac提到自己拥有IMSAI 8080设备，并讲述了其教授不建议他从事计算机职业的故事。
• **Altair 8800的价格与复刻版**：danbruc对比了Altair 8800当年的价格和如今在eBay上的售价，并提到现在有售价150美元的迷你复刻版。
• **其他早期计算机的提及**：jodydonetti提到Olivetti P101（1965），oldnetguy则认为Kenbak 1才是第一台个人计算机，dcassett补充了Mark-8这个早期的"套件计算机"。

补充讨论：
• **对微软诞生历史的影响**：igtztorrero强调了Altair 8800对微软创立的重要影响，提到比尔·盖茨和保罗·艾伦如何在Altair 8800上开发BASIC语言，并促成了微软的诞生。
• **个人捐赠经历**：vondur提到自己从岳父那里得到了Altair 8800并捐赠给了当地大学。
• **对早期PC的认知**：berlinbrowndev表示自己原以为TRS和Commodore 64才是最早的个人电脑，显示出对Altair 8800作为早期PC代表的不了解。

争议焦点：
• **最早的个人计算机之争**：在提到Altair 8800时，有人认为它是第一台个人计算机，但oldnetguy提出Kenbak 1更早，而dcassett则补充了Mark-8这个早期的"套件计算机"，显示出对"第一台个人计算机"定义的不同看法。

总结来看，评论主要围绕Altair 8800的历史地位、技术细节、相关模拟器及其对个人计算机历史的影响展开讨论，同时掺杂了一些个人经历和相关早期计算机的提及。

data.title: A Common Lisp jq replacement
data.author: tmtvl
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了作者对工具 **jq** 的不满，尤其是其复杂的特定领域语言（DSL）。作者认为 jq 的成功主要由于缺乏竞争和使用惯性，而非其实际易用性。因此，作者决定用自己熟悉和喜爱的编程语言 **Common Lisp (CL)** 开发一个替代品，命名为 **cljq**。目前，cljq 只是一个非常基础的管道工具，能够将 JSON 数据解析为变量，执行任意的 Common Lisp 表达式，并将结果序列化回 stdout。作者提到使用了 **jzon** 库来处理 JSON 序列化。文章表达了作者对 jq 的不满以及用 CL 替代的决心。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于命令行处理JSON工具（尤其是jq）的优缺点及替代方案的讨论

不同观点：
• [支持jq的立场] 一些用户如[gray_-_wolf]和[adamgordonbell]认为，尽管jq的DSL（领域特定语言）有些晦涩，但一旦掌握基础知识，它是非常有效的工具，特别是在流处理和常见的JSON操作场景下。其广泛的安装基础（如在Jenkins中预装）也是一个巨大优势。

• [批评jq的立场] 用户如[ilyash]和[forty]认为jq的DSL不够直观，过于复杂，且嵌套数据处理需要多行命令，显得笨重。他们认为现代shell应内置对结构化数据处理的支持，而无需依赖像jq这样的外部工具。

• [jq替代方案] 多个用户提出了jq的替代品：
  - [cube2222]开发了jql，一个具有lisp语法的jq替代工具，并认为其更符合个人需求。
  - [behnamoh]提到cljq，认为其在某些情况下比jq更直观。
  - [vindarel]和[diggan]分别提到了lqn和Jet，这些工具利用Clojure语法进行查询和转换，对于熟悉Clojure的用户更为友好。
  - [peterohler]推荐oj，一个基于JSONPath的JSON处理工具。
  
• [使用新技术的立场] 用户如[account-5]表示，使用Nushell替代jq进行数据处理，认为其技术更为先进，且使用体验更好。

• [AI辅助编程的立场] 用户[selkin]和[adamgordonbell]提到，借助LLM（如AI生成代码），用户不再需要深入学习jq或其他DSL，AI可以快速生成所需的查询或表达式，从而降低学习特定工具DSL的必要性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要在于jq的DSL复杂性和是否值得投入时间学习。部分用户认为其复杂性带来了不必要的学习成本，而另一些用户则认为其功能强大，值得学习。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，AI技术的兴起使得一些用户不再倾向于深入学习特定的DSL，而是依赖AI生成代码，这可能对工具的长期使用和社区发展产生影响。

总结：讨论围绕jq的优缺点展开，涉及其DSL复杂性、替代工具、以及AI辅助编程的影响。用户对是否值得学习jq及其替代方案有不同看法，反映了在命令行处理JSON工具选择上的多样化需求。

data.title: Show HN: Blast – Fast, multi-threaded serving engine for web browsing AI agents
data.author: calebhwin
data.article_summary: BLAST是一个高性能的网络浏览AI服务引擎，提供与OpenAI兼容的API，支持自动缓存和并行化，确保低成本和低延迟。它具备流式传输、并发处理等功能，可用于将网络浏览AI集成到应用中，或自动化工作流。用户可以通过`pip install blastai`快速启动，并在本地运行以节省资源。BLAST采用MIT许可证，支持多用户高效资源管理，并提供详细文档和贡献指南。主要技术栈包括Python、TypeScript、HTML、CSS和JavaScript。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个名为BLAST的工具的用途、技术实现及其伦理和实际应用问题

不同观点：
• **关于工具的技术细节和用途的困惑**：
  - [smcleod] 不确定这个工具是用于MCP服务器、浏览器引擎还是OpenAI兼容的LLM代理。
  - [otabdeveloper4] 阅读了所有文档后仍然不理解这个工具的具体用途。
  - [mtrovo] 不熟悉LLM API的用例，询问是否可以用于自定义产品的深度研究功能。

• **关于请求并发和伦理问题的讨论**：
  - [diggan] 关注工具是否采取措施避免对网站发出过多请求，是否读取rate-limit头部或在网站响应变慢时进行回退，并提出是否存在伦理考虑。
  
• **关于反bot机制和用户代理的讨论**：
  - [xena] 询问如何阻止该服务，是否读取robots.txt并拥有可识别的用户代理。
  - [gitroom] 质疑这种工具是否会超越所有反bot机制。

• **关于缓存和匹配策略的技术讨论**：
  - [adrmtu] 对前缀缓存的工作原理、页面结构变化时的无效策略以及如何匹配任务到正确的缓存前缀感兴趣。
  
• **关于工具实现库的讨论**：
  - [pal9000i] 提到使用Google时立即被验证码拦截，询问是否使用playwright或patchright。
  - [TheTaytay] 对工具默认使用的AI驱动浏览器库感到好奇，并询问是否使用"browser-use"。

• **关于高并发下资源竞争和隔离的讨论**：
  - [badmonster] 关注BLAST如何处理高并发下的浏览器实例隔离和资源竞争。

• **关于工具应用场景的讨论**：
  - [grahamgooch] 询问是否可以用于大规模web应用的自动化测试和负载测试。

• **关于动作抽象和DOM解析的讨论**：
  - [lgiordano_notte] 关注工具如何处理动作抽象，并提到通过语义解析DOM来提取高层次意图的实践。

补充讨论：
• **名称冲突问题**：
  - [debo_] 提到BLAST在生物序列比对领域已经是一个知名名称，指出可能的名称冲突问题。

争议焦点：
• 工具的用途和具体技术实现不够清晰，导致用户困惑。
• 高并发请求可能对目标网站造成压力，以及由此引发的伦理考虑。
• 如何有效绕过反bot机制同时遵循网络爬虫的道德规范。

data.author: msarnowicz
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Ubicloud如何通过利用Linux cgroups v2实现“burstable VMs”（突发型虚拟机），以降低云计算成本。传统专用虚拟机价格较高，而burstable VMs允许在共享CPU上运行，并在需要时临时提升CPU使用率，适合处理偶发的使用高峰。文章详细解释了cgroups的层次结构和工作原理，包括如何通过虚拟文件系统或systemd配置cgroups，以设置资源限制和管理CPU使用。Ubicloud利用这些特性创建了开源的突发型VM解决方案，为用户提供更经济高效的云计算选择。

Maciek Sarnowicz
Contributor
Ubicloud is an open source alternative to AWS. You can self-host our software or use our managed service to reduce your cloud costs by 3x.Â
â
Some of our customers told us that the price of dedicated VMs was too steep and asked for a lower entry point. We looked into it and came up with
burstable VMs
. These VMs run on a fraction of a shared CPU and burst to a higher level of CPU usage to support occasional spikes in usage.
To implement burstable VMs, we leveraged Linux
Control Groups v2
(cgroups v2), a Linux kernel feature that helps manage resource usage. We thought our open-source implementation of burstable VMs might be interesting enough to write about. We also learned a lot about Linux cgroups in the process!
The building blocks
Linux cgroups are organized hierarchically. Each group acts as a âcontainerâ that can host child groups, processes, and threads. These groups control specific system usage, such as cpu, io, memory, hugetlb, pids, and rdma. You can also configure cpusets to control the cpu and memory placement of Linux processes.
At each group level, you can enable specific
controllers
to set resource limits. These resource limits apply to the groupâs children (other groups and processes) and also make that controller available to the childrenâs groups.
For example, if we enable the memory controller for a group called "webservices", we can set a memory limit of 4GB for this group. Then, any processes within this group will share this 4GB allocation. We could further create child groups like "webservices/frontend" with 1.5GB and "webservices/backend" with 2.5GB, distributing the parent's resources among children.
You can use cgroups either through the virtual filesystem or through Linuxâs system manager (systemd). However, not all of cgroupâs functionality is exposed through systemd. In particular, the CPU burst settings are not.
Cgroups through a virtual filesystem
You can inspect the Control Group hierarchy and configuration through a virtual filesystem mounted at
/sys/fs/cgroup
. Key files include:
cgroup.controllers:
Lists all available controllers
cgroup.subtree_control:
Defines controllers selected for this cgroup and its descendants
cpuset.*:
Configuration files for the cpuset controller
cpu.*:
Configuration files for the CPU controller
Most of these files are writable, allowing you to modify configuration settings as needed.
Cgroups through systemd
In the systemd world, control groups manifest as
slices
- logical units for managing system resources. By default, systemd already organizes processes into predefined slices like
system.slice
and
user.slice
, creating a natural hierarchy.
We can extend this organization by creating our own custom slice for resource management. For instance, imagine we want to isolate and control resources for a CPU-intensive workload:
Our slice definition is remarkably simple:
# /etc/systemd/system/example.slice
[S
lice
]
The service that will live within our slice:
# /etc/systemd/system/stress.service
[S
ervice
]
Slice=example.slice
ExecStart=stress-ng --cpu
1
--cpu-load
50
--cpu-load-slice
100

data.title: Show HN: GPT-2 implemented using graphics shaders
data.author: nathan-barry
data.article_summary: 该项目是一个基于浏览器、使用WebGL2实现的GPT-2模型，支持transformer模块和注意力矩阵的可视化。主要特性包括通过WebGL2着色器在GPU上执行GPT-2前向传播，使用js-tiktoken进行BPE tokenization，以及一个用于下载预训练权重的简单Python脚本。项目依赖Node.js、Python和支持WebGL2的现代浏览器。前端使用Vite搭建，通过运行`npm run dev`启动本地开发服务器。项目结构清晰，包含GPT-2权重的二进制文件和相关配置文件，核心代码使用TypeScript编写。该项目已获得MIT许可证。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

GPT-2 WebGL Inference Demo
A browser-based, WebGL2 implementation of GPT-2.
🚀 Features
Full GPT-2 small (117M) forward pass in the GPU via WebGL2 shaders
BPE tokenization using
js-tiktoken
in the browser (no WASM fetch)
Simple Python script to download the pretrained weights
📋 Prerequisites
Node.js
≥ 16.x and
npm
Python
≥ 3.8
A modern browser with WebGL2 support (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
🐍 Download the GPT-2 Weights
We rely on HuggingFace’s
transformers
to pull down the official GPT-2 weights and emit raw
Float32Array
blobs:
Install Python dependencies:
pip install torch numpy transformers
Run the downloader:
python download_weights.py
This will fetch:
wte.bin
(token embeddings)
wpe.bin
(positional embeddings)
c_attn_q_w_0.bin
…
c_attn_q_w_11.bin
c_attn_k_w_0.bin
… etc.
lm_head_w.bin
,
lm_head_b.bin
And a generated
manifest.json
mapping names → URLs
⚙️  Front-end Setup with Vite
We use Vite to bundle TS, serve ESM modules & handle
js-tiktoken
:
Install JS dependencies:
npm install
Start the local dev server:
npm run dev
Open your browser at
http://localhost:5173
Any changes under
src/
will trigger HMR and live-reload.

data.title: The History of Album Art
data.author: tobr
data.article_summary: 文章简要介绍了唱片封面的起源和发展。早期唱片仅以实用性包装为主，没有专门的封面设计。随着唱片销售增长，哥伦比亚唱片公司开始将单曲捆绑销售，形成类似相册的“唱片专辑”。技术的进步使得唱片容量和材质不断提升。然而，封面艺术的诞生则是由设计师亚历克斯·斯坦因韦斯推动的，他于1948年为哥伦比亚唱片设计了首张具有视觉吸引力的专辑封面，开创了唱片作为多感官体验的先河。斯坦因韦斯深受其导师约瑟夫·宾德的大胆图形风格影响，设计了数百张经典封面，将唱片从单纯的音频媒介转变为视觉艺术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：专辑封面艺术的历史、影响及其相关轶事

不同观点：
• TheOtherHobbes 提到了几个重要的专辑封面设计师及其作品，包括ECM爵士标签的Barbara Wojirsch、Hypgnosis的Aubrey Powell和Storm Thorgerson（曾为Pink Floyd设计封面），以及Factory Records和Pete Saville的经典设计。Thorgerson被形容为一个才华横溢但性格糟糕的人。
• ChrisMarshallNY 分享了一个关于Eagles专辑封面背后故事的轶事，指出封面中的鸟骷髅下的“雪”实际上是可卡因。
• julianeon 认为由于黑胶唱片的盈利能力，专辑封面艺术将会继续存在，并引用了2023年美国非数字音乐格式收入的数据来支持这一观点。
• MassPikeMike 对专辑封面历史的讨论表示赞赏，但指出其对20世纪50到70年代这个“黄金时代”的覆盖有限，推荐了“Album Cover Album”系列书籍作为补充。
• gwbas1c 纠正了一个关于早期唱片材质的错误，指出在20世纪初，唱片是由醋酸纤维制成的，而不是乙烯基。

43872625.article_content:
Album art didn’t always exist.
In the early 1900s, recorded music was still a novelty, overshadowed by sales of sheet music. Early vinyl records were vastly different from what we think of today: discs were sold individually and could only hold up to four minutes of music per side. Sometimes, only one side of the record was used. One of the most popular records of 1910, for example, was “Come, Josephine, in My Flying Machine”: it clocked in at two minutes and 39 seconds.
An example of early album art
via
Wikipedia
The packaging of these records was strictly utilitarian: a brown paper sleeve to protect the record from dust, printed with the name of the record label or the retailer. Rarely did the packaging include any information on the disc inside; the label on the center of the disc was all there was to differentiate one record from another.
But as record sales started to show signs of life, music publishers took note. Columbia Records, one of the first companies to sell music on discs, was especially successful. They pioneered the sale of songs in bundles: the individual discs were bound together in packages resembling photo albums, partly to protect the delicate shellac that the records were made of, partly to increase their sales. They resembled photo albums, so Columbia called them “record albums.”
There were many more technological breakthroughs that made it possible to mass-manufacture and distribute music throughout the world at affordable prices. The five-minute-long 78 rpm discs were replaced by 20-minute discs that ran at 33 ⅓ rpm, which were replaced by the hour-long 12″ LP we know today. Delicate shellac was replaced by the more resilient (and cheaper) vinyl. Both recording technology and consumer electronics were always evolving, allowing more dynamic music to fit into smaller packages and be played on smaller, higher-fidelity stereos.
The invention of album art can get lost in the story of technological mastery. But among all the factors that contributed to the rise of recorded music, it stands as one of the few that was wholly driven by creators themselves. Album art — first as marketing material, then as pure creative expression — turned an audio-only medium into a multi-sensory experience.
This is the story of the people who made music visible.
The prophet: Alex Steinweiss
Alex Steinweiss was born in 1917, the son of eastern European immigrants.
Growing up in Brooklyn, New York, Steinweiss took an early interest in art and earned a scholarship to Parsons School of Design. On graduating, he worked for Austrian designer Joseph Binder, whose bold, graphic posters had influenced design for the first decades of the 1900s.
Joseph Binder,
The Most Important Wheels in America, Association of American Railroads
(1952)
via Moma
Joseph Binder,
Österreichs Wiederaufbau Ausstellung Salzburg
(1933)
via Moma
Joseph Binder,
Air Corps U.S. Army (Winning entry for the MoMA National Defense Poster Competition [Army Air Corps Recruiting])
via Moma
After his work with Binder, Steinweiss was hired by Columbia Records to produce promotional displays and ads, but the job didn’t stick. At the outbreak of World War II, he went to work for the Navy’s Training and Development Center in New York City, designing teaching material and cautionary posters.
When the war ended, Steinweiss went back to freelancing for Columbia. At a lunch meeting in 1948, company president Ted Wallerstein mentioned that Columbia would soon introduce a new kind of record that, spinning at a slower speed of 33 ⅓ rpm, could hold more music than the older 78 rpm discs. But there was a problem: the smaller, more intricate grooves on the discs were being damaged by the heavy paper sleeves used for the 78s. After the lunch, Steinweiss went to work to create a new, safer jacket for the records. But his vision for the new packaging went beyond just its construction.
“The way records were sold was ridiculous,” Steinweiss said. “The covers were brown, tan or green paper. They were not attractive, and lacked sales appeal.” He suggested that Columbia should spend more money on packaging, convinced that eye-catching designs would help sell records.
1
His first chance to prove his case was a 1940 compilation by the songwriters Rodgers and Hart — one of the first releases on the new microgroove 33 ⅓ records. For it, he asked the Imperial Theater (located one block west of Times Square) to change the lettering on their marquee to read “SMASH SONG HITS BY RODGERS & HART." Steinweiss had a photographer take a photo, and back in his studio, superimposed “COLUMBIA RECORDS’’ on the image to match the perspective and style of the signage. The last touch, a nod to the graphic abstraction of his mentor Joseph Binder, were orange lines arcing around the marquee in the exact size of the record underneath.
Album art was born.
Steinweiss' cover art for Columbia's
Smash Song Hits by Rodgers & Hart
via
RateYourMusic

43872625.article_summary: 文章简要介绍了唱片封面的起源和发展。早期唱片仅以实用性包装为主，没有专门的封面设计。随着唱片销售增长，哥伦比亚唱片公司开始将单曲捆绑销售，形成类似相册的“唱片专辑”。技术的进步使得唱片容量和材质不断提升。然而，封面艺术的诞生则是由设计师亚历克斯·斯坦因韦斯推动的，他于1948年为哥伦比亚唱片设计了首张具有视觉吸引力的专辑封面，开创了唱片作为多感官体验的先河。斯坦因韦斯深受其导师约瑟夫·宾德的大胆图形风格影响，设计了数百张经典封面，将唱片从单纯的音频媒介转变为视觉艺术。

data.title: A proof of concept tool to verify estimates
data.author: jjgreen
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了验证渐近估计（尤其是涉及多个正实数的算术运算的不等式）的自动化工具的缺乏及其实现的可能性。作者指出，虽然符号数学软件在代数和微积分等领域很发达，但在验证渐近估计方面缺乏类似工具。作者特别关注不使用减法、仅涉及加法、乘法、除法、指数、最大值和最小值的简单渐近估计。

作者希望开发一种自动化工具，能够验证这类不等式并提供证明或反例。通过Python编程和大型语言模型的帮助，作者成功创建了一个概念验证工具，可以自动验证诸如弱算术平均-几何平均不等式等简单不等式。尽管输出的证明不够优雅，但实现了自动化验证的目标。作者提供了Github代码库链接，展示了工具的实际应用。

简而言之，本文探讨了自动化验证渐近估计的必要性和初步实现方法。

This post was inspired by some recent discussions with Bjoern Bringmann.
Symbolic math software packages are highly developed for many mathematical tasks in areas such as algebra, calculus, and numerical analysis. However, to my knowledge we do not have similarly sophisticated tools for verifying asymptotic estimates – inequalities that are supposed to hold for arbitrarily large parameters, with constant losses. Particularly important are functional estimates, where the parameters involve an unknown function or sequence (living in some suitable function space, such as an
space); but for this discussion I will focus on the simpler situation of asymptotic estimates involving a finite number of positive real numbers, combined using arithmetic operations such as addition, multiplication, division, exponentiation, and minimum and maximum (but no subtraction). A typical inequality here might be the weak arithmetic mean-geometric mean inequality

I have wished in the past (e.g.,

Any single such inequality is not too difficult to resolve by hand, but there are applications in which one needs to check a large number of such inequalities, or split into a large number of cases. I will take an example at random from an

This particular bound could be dispatched in three or four lines from some simpler inequalities; but it took some time to come up with those inequalities, and I had to do a dozen further inequalities of this type. This is a task that seems extremely ripe for automation, particularly with modern technology.
Recently, I have been doing a lot more coding (in Python, mostly) than in the past, aided by the remarkable facility of large language models to generate initial code samples for many different tasks, or to autocomplete partially written code. For the most part, I have restricted myself to fairly simple coding tasks, such as computing and then plotting some mildly complicated mathematical functions, or doing some rudimentary data analysis on some dataset. data.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: Brendan Gregg的博客文章介绍了其最新开发的GPU火焰图工具，特别是支持Intel Battlemage GPU，能够生成全栈GPU火焰图，帮助分析游戏性能问题。通过将CPU和GPU火焰图并排比较，可以直观地进行性能关联分析。文章以GZDoom游戏为例，展示了如何通过FlameScope工具选择特定时间范围生成火焰图，分析CPU和GPU的工作负载。GPU火焰图中不同颜色代表不同的指令和代码路径，帮助识别性能瓶颈，如渲染墙壁、后期处理效果等。此外，文章提到通过构建更复杂的游戏地图和调整GPU资源设置，成功增加了GZDoom的性能需求以进行更深入的测试。

Doom GPU Flame Graphs
01 May 2025
AI Flame Graphs
are now
open source
and include Intel Battlemage GPU support, which means it can also generate full-stack GPU flame graphs for providing new insights into gaming performance, especially when coupled with
FlameScope
(an older open source project of mine). Here's an example of GZDoom, and I'll start with flame scopes for both CPU and GPU utilization, with details annotated:
(Here are the raw
CPU
and
GPU
versions.) FlameScope shows a subsecond-offset heatmap of profile samples, where each column is one second (in this example, made up of 50 x 20ms blocks) and the color depth represents the number of samples, revealing variance and perturbation that you can select to generate a flame graph just for that time range.
Putting these CPU and GPU flame scopes side by side has enabled your eyes to do pattern matching to solve what would otherwise be a time-consuming task of performance correlation. The gaps in the GPU flame scope on the right – where the GPU was not doing much work – match the heavier periods of CPU work on the left.
CPU Analysis
FlameScope lets us click on the interesting periods. By selecting one of the CPU shader compilation stripes we get the flame graph just for that range:
This is brilliant, and we can see exactly why the CPUs were busy for about 180 ms (the vertical length of the red stripe): it's doing compilation of GPU shaders and some NIR preprocessing (optimizations to the
NIR intermediate representation
that Mesa uses internally). If you are new to flame graphs, you look for the widest towers and optimize them first. Here is the
interactive SVG
.
CPU flame graphs and CPU flame scope aren't new (from
2011
and
2018
, both open source). What is new is full-stack
GPU
flame graphs and
GPU
flame scope.
GPU Analysis
Interesting details can also be selected in the GPU FlameScope for generating GPU flame graphs.
This example selects the "room 3" range, which is a room in the Doom map that contains hundreds of enemies.
The
green
frames are the actual instructions running on the GPU,
aqua
shows the source for these functions, and
red
(C) and
yellow
(C++) show the CPU code paths that initiated the GPU programs. The
gray
"-" frames just help highlight the boundary between CPU and GPU code. (This is similar to what I described in the
AI flame graphs
post, which included extra frames for kernel code.) The x-axis is proportional to cost, so you look for the widest things and find ways to reduce them.
I've included the
interactive SVG
version of this flame graph so you can mouse-over elements and click to zoom. (
PNG
version.)
The GPU flame graph is split between stalls coming from rendering walls (41.4%), postprocessing effects (35.7%), stenciling (17.2%), and sprites (4.95%). The CPU stacks are further differentiated by the individual shaders that are causing stalls, along with the reasons for those stalls.
GZDoom
We picked
GZDoom
to try since it's an open source version of a well known game that runs on Linux (our profiler does not support Windows yet). Intel Battlemage makes light work of GZDoom, however, and since the GPU profile is stall-based we weren't getting many samples. We could have switched to a more modern and GPU-demanding game, but didn't have any great open source ideas, so I figured we'd just make GZDoom more demanding. We built GPU demanding maps for GZDoom (I can't believe I have found a work-related reason to be using
Slade
), and also set some Battlemage tunables to limit resources, magnifying the utilization of remaining resources.

43858183.article_summary: Brendan Gregg的博客文章介绍了其最新开发的GPU火焰图工具，特别是支持Intel Battlemage GPU，能够生成全栈GPU火焰图，帮助分析游戏性能问题。通过将CPU和GPU火焰图并排比较，可以直观地进行性能关联分析。文章以GZDoom游戏为例，展示了如何通过FlameScope工具选择特定时间范围生成火焰图，分析CPU和GPU的工作负载。GPU火焰图中不同颜色代表不同的指令和代码路径，帮助识别性能瓶颈，如渲染墙壁、后期处理效果等。此外，文章提到通过构建更复杂的游戏地图和调整GPU资源设置，成功增加了GZDoom的性能需求以进行更深入的测试。

data.title: Derivation and Intuition behind Poisson distribution
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Poisson分布及其应用和相关悖论

不同观点：
• [quirino] 提出并解释了“等待时间悖论”（Waiting Time Paradox）。他指出，在随机时刻采样时，平均间隔似乎是20分钟，而按事件间隔采样时平均是10分钟，强调了采样方式对结果的影响。
• [meatmanek] 讨论了Poisson分布在排队理论中的应用，认为它类似于正态分布在统计学中的地位。他提供了两个主要原因：Poisson分布是对独立用户请求到达系统的一种良好近似，并且它使数学计算变得可行，可以得出例如平均等待时间等闭式解。
• [Rant423] 提供了一个1946年关于Poisson分布应用的论文链接，展示了Poisson分布的历史应用。
• [mmorse1217] 分享了一个技术性较强的网站链接，认为该网站对理解Poisson分布有帮助。
• [firesteelrain] 提到在工作中使用Arena软件建模时，Poisson分布是他们的首选分布，强调了Poisson分布在实际工作中的应用价值。
• [hammock] 认为Poisson分布、Pareto分布、正态分布是其最重要的三种分布，并指出这些分布常常被误用，强调了正确选择分布的重要性。

补充讨论：
• [joe_the_user] 偏离了Poisson分布的讨论，转而抱怨某个网站的JavaScript永久重定向问题，认为这种做法不友好。
• [cwmoore] 简单提到灯泡烧毁的时间问题，可能是在暗示Poisson分布在寿命预测中的应用，但未展开讨论。
• [digger495] 和 [DAGdug] 的评论较为简短，未对Poisson分布提供实质性的讨论或贡献。

争议焦点：
• 主要的争议点集中在“等待时间悖论”的理解上，即为什么在随机时刻采样时平均间隔是20分钟，而按事件间隔采样时平均是10分钟。这涉及到采样方式对统计结果的影响。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• Poisson分布在实际应用中的重要性，尤其是在排队理论和系统建模中的应用。
• 不同分布（Poisson、Pareto、正态分布）的正确选择和常见误用。
• 提供了多个关于Poisson分布的学习资源和应用实例链接。

总结：评论主要围绕Poisson分布的理论探讨、实际应用及其相关悖论展开，同时提供了一些有用的资源和实际工作中的使用经验。

data.title: Relational Graph Transformers
data.author: gk1
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了**关系图变换器（Relational Graph Transformers）**，一种用于从关系数据库中提取情报的突破性架构。传统机器学习方法难以处理跨多个表格的复杂数据关系，而关系图变换器通过将关系数据库转化为图结构，使得人工智能系统能够更有效地学习和导航这些数据，无需繁琐的特征工程和复杂的数据管道。

关键优势包括：
1. 比传统方法快20倍的价值实现时间。
2. 通过更深入理解关系背景，准确性提高30-50%。
3. 数据准备工作量减少95%。

该方法分为三个步骤：
1. 理解关系数据库结构。
2. 创建模式图（schema graph），表作为节点，外键关系作为边。
3. 构建关系实体图（relational entity graph），行作为节点，外键链接作为边。

这种方法特别适合企业数据分析，已在客户分析、推荐系统、欺诈检测和需求预测等领域得到应用。关系图变换器为数据科学家和企业领导者提供了强大的工具，重新定义了AI如何与业务数据交互。

43824297.article_content:
In the world of enterprise data, the most valuable insights often lie not in individual tables, but in the complex relationships between them. Customer interactions, product hierarchies, transaction histories—these interconnected data points tell rich stories that traditional machine learning approaches struggle to fully capture. Enter
Relational Graph Transformers
: a breakthrough architecture that's transforming how we extract intelligence from relational databases.
Relational Graph Transformers represent the next evolution in
Relational Deep Learning
, allowing AI systems to seamlessly navigate and learn from data spread across multiple tables. By treating relational databases as the rich, interconnected graphs they inherently are, these models eliminate the need for extensive feature engineering and complex data pipelines that have traditionally slowed AI adoption.
This isn't just an incremental improvement—it's a fundamental rethinking of how AI interacts with business data, delivering remarkable results:
20x faster time-to-value compared to traditional approaches
30-50% accuracy improvements through deeper understanding of relational context
95% reduction in data preparation effort
In this post, we'll explore how Relational Graph Transformers work, why they're uniquely suited for enterprise data challenges, and how they're already revolutionizing applications from customer analytics and recommendation systems to fraud detection and demand forecasting.
Whether you're a data scientist looking to push the boundaries of what's possible, or a business leader seeking to unlock the full potential of your organization's data assets, Relational Graph Transformers represent a powerful new tool in your AI toolkit.
This post is part of a series about Graph Transformers. If you want to learn more about Graph Transformers in the wild, see our previous post
“An Introduction to Scalable Graph Transformers”
.
From Relational Database to Graphs
Relational databases are one of the most common data formats in the world, especially in business settings. They store information in a structured format across multiple
tables
, with
foreign key relationships
defining how entities in one table relate to those in another. While traditional ML models often struggle to extract meaningful patterns from such multi-table setups,
Relational Deep Learning
re-frames the problem: instead of flattening tables into feature vectors, we
transform the entire database into a graph
—a format much more expressive for learning complex relationships.
Let’s break this transformation down step by step.
Step 1: Understanding the Relational Database
We start with a database defined by a set of
tables
and a set of
links
that describe foreign key relationships between tables. Each link indicates that a foreign key in one table points to the primary key in another.
Each
row
in a table is treated as an
entity
with four components:
A
primary key
that uniquely identifies it.
A set of
foreign keys
linking it to rows in other tables.
A set of
attributes
containing its descriptive content (
e.g.
, name, price, image).
An optional
timestamp
if the row records an event over time.
Step 2: Creating the Schema Graph
Before jumping to the entity-level graph, we first construct a
schema graph
—a high-level blueprint of the database. In this graph,
nodes
are tables, and
edges
represent foreign key relationships (and their inverses), ensuring every table is reachable. This schema graph helps define the
types
of nodes and edges that will appear in the next step: the entity graph.
Step 3: Building the Relational Entity Graph
Now, we construct the
relational entity graph
, where:
Each
node
corresponds to a row (entity) in the database.
Each
edge
connects entities based on foreign key links.
This graph is
heterogeneous
: each node and edge is typed based on the schema graph, allowing models to distinguish between, say, a
Customer
node and a
Product
node, or between a
purchased
edge and a
viewed
edge.
By turning the relational database into a richly structured graph, we enable
deep learning models to reason directly over the underlying relationships
—without flattening, joins, or feature engineering. This transformation preserves the semantics of the original data, respects its structure, and supports heterogeneous and temporal modeling out of the box.
This is the foundation on which
Relational Graph Transformers
operate: a graph-native, schema-aware, and modality-flexible input space that unlocks the full expressive power of deep learning for relational data.
(a) Schema graph: tables as nodes, edges from foreign key links. (b) Entity graph: individual rows as nodes, connected via schema-defined edges with timestamps for temporal context.

data.title: Strings Just Got Faster
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 在JDK 25中，String类的性能得到了改进，特别是String::hashCode函数现在可以大部分实现常量折叠。这使得在使用String作为键的静态不可变Map中，可以显著提升性能。改进的核心在于String的hash码在首次计算后会被缓存，并通过@Stable注解告知虚拟机该字段不会再改变，从而实现常量折叠。这一优化对任何使用不可变Map<String, V>的场景都有效，特别是在键为常量字符串时。不过，当String的hash码为零时，该优化无法生效，因为常量折叠只对非默认值有效。虽然@Stable注解目前仅限于JDK内部使用，但正在开发的JEP 502将允许用户代码间接受益。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Java字符串性能改进及相关技术细节

不同观点：
• **[smcin]** 认为文章标题具有误导性，建议标题应强调JDK 25中的性能改进，而不是泛指所有Java字符串的改进。
• **[stevoski]** 对Java字符串类的历史性能改进表示赞赏，认为尽管早期的改进较为显著，但如今的改进对实际应用的影响可能有限。
• **[gavinray]** 对新引入的JEP 502 "Stable Values"感到困惑，尤其是它与Records和Value Classes的区别，不理解它们在功能上的差异。
• **[theanonymousone]** 认为字符串类型的改进将对性能产生重大影响，甚至可能影响全球碳足迹。
• **[int_19h]** 关注JVM中字符串哈希未随机化的问题，推测可能是为了保持向后兼容性。

补充讨论：
• **[daxfohl]** 对文章中的具体性能改进示例表示困惑，尤其是关于MethodHandle和不可变映射的细节，质疑是否所有场景都能看到类似的性能提升。
• **[koliber]** 简单总结了文章内容，认为是对hashCode()函数的 memoization（记忆化）改进。
• **[vault]** 抱怨技术文章中代码块的排版问题，特别是引号和其他特殊符号的使用。
• **[ashvardanian]** 关注JNI调用延迟的基准测试，并询问是否有人分享过相关数据，因为这影响到将字符串库引入JVM生态系统的可行性。
• **[jbverschoor]** 对字符串哈希码是否在编译时计算表示疑问，并联想到Ruby的符号（symbols）。
• **[layer8]** 指出JEP 502的新模式虽然引入了性能改进，但也会导致每个“stable”字段额外创建一个对象，这可能不符合懒初始化的初衷。
• **[rf15]** 认为专门为字符串做一篇改进文章有些奇怪，因为这实际上是基于@Stable注解的工作成果。
• **[esafak]** 询问Kotlin和Scala是否能从这些改进中受益。
• **[kazinator]** 分享了自己在TXR Lisp中对字符串哈希码的实验，并认为在某些情况下，缓存哈希值并不是必要的，因为表达式可以直接折叠优化。

争议焦点：
• Java字符串哈希码是否应该随机化，以及JVM为了兼容性未实现哈希随机化的合理性。
• 新引入的"Stable Values"与Records、Value Classes的功能差异及其实际应用场景。
• 字符串性能改进对实际应用的影响大小，尤其是在现代Java应用中是否显著。

这些观点反映了社区对Java字符串性能改进的不同关注点和技术细节的深入探讨。

43854337.article_content:
Strings Just Got Faster
Per-Ake Minborg
on
May  1, 2025
In JDK 25,
we improved
the performance of the class
String
in such a way that the
String::hashCode
function is mostly
constant foldable
. For example, if you use Strings as keys in a static unmodifiable
Map
, you will likely see significant performance improvements.
Example
Here is a relatively advanced example where we maintain an immutable
Map
of native calls, its keys are the name of the method call and the values are a
MethodHandle
that can be used to invoke the associated system call:
// Set up an immutable Map of system calls
static
final
Map
<
String
,
MethodHandle
>
SYSTEM_CALLS
=
Map
.
of
(
“
malloc
”
,
linker
.
downcallHandle
(
mallocSymbol
,
…
),
“
free
”
,
linker
.
downcallHandle
(
freeSymbol
…
),
...);
…
// Allocate a memory region of 16 bytes
long
address
=
SYSTEM_CALLS
.
get
(
“
malloc
”
).
invokeExact
(
16L
);
…
// Free the memory region
SYSTEM_CALLS
.
get
(
“
free
”
).
invokeExact
(
address
);
The method
linker.downcallHandle(…)
takes a symbol and additional parameters to bind a native call to a Java
MethodHandle
via the
Foreign Function & Memory API
introduced in JDK 22. This is a relatively slow process and involves spinning bytecode. However, once entered into the
Map
, the new performance improvements in the
String
class alone allow constant folding of both the key lookups and the values, thus improving performance by a factor of more than 8x:
--- JDK 24 ---
Benchmark                     Mode  Cnt  Score   Error  Units
StringHashCodeStatic.nonZero  avgt   15  4.632 ± 0.042  ns/op
--- JDK 25 ---
Benchmark                     Mode  Cnt  Score   Error  Units
StringHashCodeStatic.nonZero  avgt   15  0.571 ± 0.012  ns/op
Note
: the benchmarks above are not using a
malloc()
MethodHandle
but an
int
identity function
. After all, we are not testing the performance of
malloc()
but the actual
String
lookup and
MethodHandle
performance.
This improvement will benefit any immutable
Map<String, V>
with Strings as keys and where values (of arbitrary type
V
) are looked up via constant Strings.
How Does It Work?
When a
String
is first created, its hashcode is unknown. On the first call to
String::hashCode
, the actual hashcode is computed and stored in a private field
String.hash
. This transformation might sound odd; if
String
is
immutable
, how can it mutate its state? The answer is that the mutation cannot be observed from the outside;
String
would functionally behave the same regardless of whether or not an internal
String.hash
cache field is used. The only difference is that it becomes faster for subsequent calls.
Now that we know how
String::hashCode
works, we can unveil the performance changes made (which consists of a single line of code): the internal field
String.hash
is marked with the JDK-internal
@Stable
annotation. That’s it!
@Stable
tells the virtual machine it can read the field once and, if it is no longer its default value (zero), it can trust the field never change again. Hence, it can
constant-fold
the
String::hashcode
operation and replace the call with the known
hash
. As it turns out, the fields in the immutable
Map
and the internals of the
MethodHandle
are also trusted in the same way. This means the virtual machine can constant-fold the entire chain of operations:
Computing the hash code of the String “malloc” (which is always
-1081483544
)
Probing the immutable
Map
(i.e., compute the internal array index which is always the same for the
malloc
hashcode)
Retrieving the associated
MethodHandle
(which always resides on said computed index)
Resolving the actual native call (which is always the native
malloc()
call)
In effect, this means the native
malloc()
method call can be invoked directly, which explains the tremendous performance improvements. To put it in other words, the chain of operation is completely short-circuited.
What Are the Ifs and Buts?
There is an unfortunate corner case that the new improvement does not cover: if the hash code of the
String
happens to be zero, constant folding will not work. As we learned above, constant folding can only take place for non-default values (i.e., non-zero values for
int
fields). However, we anticipate we will be able to fix this small impediment in the near future. You might think only one in about 4 billion distinct Strings has a hash code of zero and that might be right in the average case. However, one of the most common strings (the empty string “”) has a hash value of zero. On the other hand, no string with 1 - 6 characters (inclusive) (all characters ranging from ` ` (space) to
Z
) has a hash code that is zero.
A Final Note
As
@Stable
annotation is applicable only to internal JDK code, you cannot use it directly in your Java applications. However, we are working on a new JEP called
JEP 502: Stable Values (Preview)
that will provide constructs that allow user code to indirectly benefit from
@Stable
fields in a similar way.
What’s the Next Step?
You can
download JDK 25
alr

data.title: "Silent Spring" remains a rousing call to action (2022)
data.author: simonebrunozzi
data.article_summary: 《寂静的春天》是蕾切尔·卡森1962年出版的具有里程碑意义的环境书籍，以一个寓言故事开头，描述了一个曾经与自然和谐相处的小镇因人类活动而陷入死寂。这本书揭露了农药对环境的危害，唤醒了公众的环保意识，推动了美国现代环境保护运动的发展。书中强调人类对自然的破坏，呼吁采取行动保护地球。该书影响深远，至今仍具有警示意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于纪录片《Common Ground》的观后感以及对DDT等化学物质的使用和规制的讨论

不同观点：
• **luckman212的观点**：认为《Common Ground》这部纪录片质量较高，虽然令人感到不安，但提出通过提高公众意识，未来仍有希望。这表明他对环境问题持一种谨慎乐观的态度，强调教育和意识提高的重要性。

• **HocusLocus的观点**：关注DDT从广泛使用到被完全禁用的历史转变，并提出疑问，为什么DDT被彻底禁用，而其他内分泌干扰物质却仍在使用。他提出一个心理学上的解释，认为人们喜欢将某个有害物质塑造成“化学希特勒”，然后集中精力消除它，以显示问题的解决，而不必对其他仍在使用的有害物质做出解释。这暗示他对DDT的禁用政策持怀疑态度，认为其中可能有社会心理因素在作祟。

补充讨论：
• **mikestew的观点**：没有发表具体评论，仅提供了一个存档链接（archive.ph/17T6Q），可能意在提供相关背景资料或供其他讨论者参考。

争议焦点：
• DDT的禁用政策是否合理，以及为何其他类似的有害化学物质未被同等对待。HocusLocus对DDT被“妖魔化”表示质疑，认为其中可能有社会心理因素，而非 purely 科学依据。这与luckman212对环境问题通过提高意识可以改善的乐观态度形成对比。

• 公众对环境问题的意识和行动之间的关系。luckman212认为提高公众意识是解决环境问题的关键，而HocusLocus则暗示公众可能被引导去关注某些特定问题，而忽略了其他同样重要的问题。

总的来说，讨论围绕环境纪录片的启示以及特定化学物质的规制历史展开，重点在于政策背后的科学与社会心理因素。

data.title: Converting a Git repo from tabs to spaces (2016)
data.author: keybored
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者如何将Yelp的主要Python代码库从使用制表符（tabs）转换为空格（spaces）的过程。由于Python生态系统普遍遵循四个空格的缩进方式，而Yelp的代码一直使用制表符，这给开发人员带来了一些困扰。在2013年底，作者决定将整个代码库从制表符转换为四个空格。文章详细介绍了转换前的准备工作，如确保不改变主意、修复不一致的缩进，以及使用Git过滤器防止新制表符进入代码库。作者还提供了具体的技术步骤和建议，如使用`compileall`模块查找缩进错误，并建议在所有人都停止工作时进行这种大规模更改，以减少冲突。文章最后强调，作者不再关心制表符与空格的争论，且无法再逆转当年的更改。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Git 中处理大规模机械性变更（如格式化、制表符与空格转换）的最佳实践及其对 `git blame` 等工具的影响

不同观点：
• mmastrac 认为 Git 应该引入一种机制，允许某些提交被标记为 "blame-free"，以避免机械性变更影响 `git blame` 的使用。他后来提到 `.git-blame-ignore-revs` 可以解决部分问题。
• rurban 则表示不需要复杂的解决方案，只需通过简单的命令执行大规模格式化变更，并认为不需要使用 `.gitattribute` 过滤器或“魔法重写”，直接提交即可。
• joshstrange 支持 mmastrac 的观点，认为大规模机械性变更会“污染” `git blame`，并且在 IDE 中查看变更历史时会感到不便，强调了 `.git-blame-ignore-revs` 的重要性。他还提到了团队中有人对破坏 `git blame` 的担忧。
• Alifatisk 对为什么要将制表符转换为空格表示不解，质疑这种操作的必要性。
• gwbas1c 提供了在 .net 生态系统中通过 `.editorconfig` 文件控制格式的方法，并建议在 GitHub Actions 中使用该配置文件以确保代码风格一致。
• zzo38computer 指出某些文件（如 Gopher 菜单和 Makefile）需要保留制表符，说明并非所有情况下都适合将制表符转换为空格。
• s09dfhks 对其他人提到的“拟人化”或“吉祥物”提交方式表示困惑和不满。
• baobun 提供了另一种使用 `find` 和 `sed` 命令处理制表符转换的简化方法。
• gwbas1c 还分享了一个因将制表符替换为空格导致测试失败的趣闻，强调了在代码中使用可见字符的重要性。
• kgwxd 对程序员普遍喜欢固定宽度字体但同时对某些字符（如制表符）有不同偏好表示不解。
• user9999999999 强烈支持使用分号作为块范围标识符，反对使用空白字符（如制表符和空格）来定义代码块。

补充讨论：

43869236.article_content:
This post is about the thing in the title.
I used to work for Yelp.  For historical reasons — probably “the initial developers preferred it” — their mostly-Python codebase had always been indented with tabs.  That’s in stark contrast to the vast majority of the Python ecosystem, which generally uses the
standard library’s style guide
recommendation of four spaces.  The presence of tabs caused occasional minor headaches and grumbles among the Python developers, who now numbered in the dozens and were generally used to spaces.
At the end of 2013, I bestowed Yelp with a Christmas gift: I converted their
entire primary codebase
from tabs to four spaces.  On the off chance anyone else ever wants to do the same, here’s how I did it.  Probably.  I mean, it’s been two and a half years, but I wrote most of this at the time, so it should be correct.
Please note: I
do not care
what you think about tabs versus spaces.
That’s for a
different
post!  I no longer work for Yelp, anyway — so as compelling as your argument may be, I can no longer undo what I have done.
Prerequisites
First,
be absolutely sure you’re never going to change your mind
.  If you as an organization are ambivalent about your whitespace needs, or if you have influential coworkers who will use this post for evil to switch everything back to tabs as soon as you leave, you may wish to reconsider.
Fix mixed indentation
If you’re using a whitespace-sensitive language, you
must
fix any inconsistent indentation.  (You might want to do this anyway, or your code will look like nonsense.)  By “inconsistent”, I mean any code that will change relative indentation levels if the width of a tab changes. Consider:
1
....if foo:
2
------->print("true")
If a tab is considered to be eight cells wide, as the good Lord intended, this is fine.  But if you’re about to replace all your tabs with four spaces, the extra indentation level vanishes, and suddenly this is invalid Python.
You would not
believe
how many cases of this I found.  I most fondly remember the file that was for some reason indented with
n
tabs
plus
a single space, except where it wasn’t.  I have no idea how that happened.  (Incidentally, the need to micromanage variable-width invisible characters is one of the reasons I wanted to get rid of tabs.)  (Please don’t leave comments about this.)  (Also consider
set shiftround
if you use vim, which pretty well eliminates this problem but is tragically under-used.)
On the other hand, if you are some kind of monster and want to replace every tab with
eight
spaces, then you don’t need to worry about this.
You could just scan your codebase for leading spaces, but if you have a mix of tabbed files and spaced files, you’ll get a ton of false positives and it’ll be a huge pain in the ass.  A somewhat more robust approach for Python specifically is:
1
python
-tt
-m
compileall
.
|
grep
Sorry
-tt
tells the interpreter to treat inconsistent indentation as a
SyntaxError
.  The
compileall
module searches recursively for
.py
files and produces
.pyc
bytecode, which requires parsing each file, which will trigger the
SyntaxError
.  And any errors encountered while compiling modules produce a line starting with
Sorry
, along with the filename, line number, and column number.
Now you can spend an afternoon fixing those all by hand and trying to figure out why this one file seems to have been written with a tabstop of 3.
Distribute a Git filter definition
The actual process uses a
Git filter
to enforce that no new tabs find their way into the repository and fix any tabs on in-flight branches.  The configuration for which filters to run on which files is stored as part of the repository, but unfortunately, the configuration for what each filter
does
is not.
One way or another, you
must
get this block in your devs’ Git configuration — anyone doing regular development who doesn’t have the filter definition will be
utterly
confused.  This is probably the hardest part of the process.  Thankfully, Yelp mostly does work on beefy shared dev machines, so I only had to bug an ops person to stick this incantation in
/etc/gitconfig
and wait for Puppet.
YMMV
.
1
[filter "spabs"]
2
clean = expand --initial -t 4
3
smudge = expand --initial -t 4
4
required
5
[merge]
6
renormalize = true
I’ll explain what this all actually does later.  Oh, and it might help to actually have
expand
installed.  Most Unix-likes should have it already; if you have developers using Windows,
expand
is one of the utilities in the
unixutils
project.  Also,
BSD
(i.e.
OS
X)
expand
apparently doesn’t have the
--initial
argument, but unless you’re in the habit of sprinkling tab characters inside string literals, you can safely leave it off.
Doing it
Here’s the good part.
If at all possible, get all your collaborators to stop doing work for a day while you get this sorted.  Christmas works pretty well!  I did this on December 26, when we were so short-staffed that there weren’t even any deploys scheduled.
Invoking Git's nuclear
43869236.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者如何将Yelp的主要Python代码库从使用制表符（tabs）转换为空格（spaces）的过程。由于Python生态系统普遍遵循四个空格的缩进方式，而Yelp的代码一直使用制表符，这给开发人员带来了一些困扰。在2013年底，作者决定将整个代码库从制表符转换为四个空格。文章详细介绍了转换前的准备工作，如确保不改变主意、修复不一致的缩进，以及使用Git过滤器防止新制表符进入代码库。作者还提供了具体的技术步骤和建议，如使用`compileall`模块查找缩进错误，并建议在所有人都停止工作时进行这种大规模更改，以减少冲突。文章最后强调，作者不再关心制表符与空格的争论，且无法再逆转当年的更改。

data.title: Achieving Human Level Competitive Robot Table Tennis
data.author: badmonster
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种达到业余人类水平的乒乓球机器人，这是通过分层和模块化的策略架构实现的。该机器人能够在真实环境中与未曾见过的对手进行实时适应，并在与人类的对抗中展现了良好的表现。在29场人机对战中，机器人赢得了45%的比赛，其中对初学者胜率达100%，对中级玩家胜率为55%。研究贡献包括：一种分层模块化策略架构，实现零样本模拟到现实的技术，对未知对手的实时适应，以及通过用户研究验证模型的有效性。机器人通过选择低级技能（如正手攻球、反手瞄准等）来应对比赛，并在模拟中进行训练，以弥补模拟与现实的差距。这一研究标志着机器人技术在高速运动、实时决策和系统设计方面的显著进步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DeepMind在机器人乒乓球项目中的表现及其技术方法的评价与争议

不同观点：
• [YeGoblynQueenne] 认为DeepMind在缩小模拟与现实差距（sim-2-real gap）方面的方法具有重要意义，尤其是在通过迭代模拟和现实调优来训练机器人策略。然而，他们对这种混合了强化学习与符号方法（neuro-symbolic approach）的技术保持低调，不明确宣传，这点令人困惑。
• [perlgeek] 从乒乓球爱好者的角度指出，机器人并未真正处理球的旋转（spin）问题，且使用的器材（如胶皮厚度）无法体现真实比赛中的复杂性。尽管如此，仍肯定了该项目在人与机器人互动方面的成就。
• [artofpongfu] 认为尽管项目成果很酷，但称其达到“人类水平”为时尚早，尤其是与顶级人类选手相比，机器人还有很大差距。同时提到虚拟现实（VR）在短期内可能比机器人学更有前景。
• [BugsJustFindMe] 质疑“业余水平”的定义，指出视频中人类对手并未尽全力，并怀疑机器人是否能应对更强的攻击。
• [huem0n] 认为该项目主要是物理与弹道学问题，而非机器学习问题，指出类似表现早在6年前就有更优的机器人，并对DeepMind的宣传方式表示不满。

Highlights

Full Length Match Videos
Achieving human-level speed and performance on real world tasks is a north star for the robotics research community. This work takes a step towards that goal and presents the first learned robot agent that reaches amateur human-level performance in competitive table tennis. Table tennis is a physically demanding sport which requires human players to undergo years of training to achieve an advanced level of proficiency. In this paper, we contribute (1) a hierarchical and modular policy architecture consisting of (i) low level controllers with their detailed skill descriptors which model the agent's capabilities and help to bridge the sim-to-real gap and (ii) a high level controller that chooses the low level skills, (2) techniques for enabling zero-shot sim-to-real including an iterative approach to defining the task distribution that is grounded in the real-world and defines an automatic curriculum, and (3) real time adaptation to unseen opponents. Policy performance was assessed through 29 robot vs. human matches of which the robot won 45% (13/29). All humans were unseen players and their skill level varied from beginner to tournament level. Whilst the robot lost all matches vs. the most advanced players it won 100% matches vs. beginners and 55% matches vs. intermediate players, demonstrating solidly amateur human-level performance.
Coach Barney Demonstrates Capabilities
Match Highlights
Truly awesome to watch the robot play players of all levels and styles. Going in our aim was to have the robot be at an intermediate level. Amazingly it did just that, all the hard work paid off.
I feel the robot exceeded even my expectations. It was a true honor and pleasure to be a part of this research. I have learned so much and am very thankful for everyone I had the pleasure of working with on this.
- Barney J. Reed, Professional Table Tennis Coach
Motivation
Achieving human-level performance in terms of accuracy, speed, and adaptability remains a challenge for robotics in spite of inspiring recent progress.
Table Tennis requires years of training for humans to master due to its complex low level skills and strategic gameplay.
A strategically suboptimal - but confidently executable - low
level skill might be a better choice. This sets
Table Tennis
apart from purely strategic games such as Chess, Go, etc.
Table Tennis is thus a valuable benchmark for advancing robotic capabilities, including high-speed motion, real-time precise and strategic decision making, system design and
enabling direct competition with a human opponent
.
No prior research in robotic Table Tennis has addressed the challenge of a robot playing a full competitive game against previously unseen humans.
Contributions
Our approach lead to
competitive play at human level and
a robot agent
that humans actually enjoy playing with
. To achieve this we
make
four
technical contributions:
A
hierarchical and modular policy architecture

R
eal time adaptation to unseen opponents

user-study to test our model playing actual matches against unseen humans in physical environments
Method
The
agent
consists of a
library of
low-level skill
s
and high-level controller that selects
the most effective skill
. Each low-level skill policy specializes in a specific aspect of table tennis, such as forehand topspin, backhand targeting, or forehand serve. In addition to
training
the policy itself, we collect and store information both offline and online about the strengths, weaknesses, and limitations of each low-level skill. The resulting
skill descriptors
provide the robot with important information regarding its abilities and shortcomings. In turn, a high-level controller, responsible for orchestrating the low-level skills, selects the optimal skill given the current game statistics, skill descriptors and the opponent's capabilities.

data.title: GitDroid: A third party Android app manager for apps uploaded to GitHub releases
data.author: amadeuspagel
data.article_summary: GitDroid 是一个第三方 Android 应用管理器，用于管理上传到 GitHub 发布的应用。该项目包含一个应用商店，专门用于获取和处理 GitHub 上的应用发布。GitDroid 主要使用 Dart 语言编写，少量使用 Java。目前有 14 个星标，但没有发布正式版本。项目托管在 GitHub 上，并接受赞助支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于不同应用管理工具的比较与使用体验，以及对移动设备生态系统的批评

不同观点：
• Cyphase认为Unobtanium比Obtainium支持更多的来源和功能，并且正在积极开发中，暗示Unobtanium更具优势。
• 0xbadcafebee强烈批评移动设备的应用商店和锁定机制，主张像传统计算机一样自由运行和安装应用程序，强调开放性和持续支持的重要性。
• Sigmonsays表达了对Obtainium的喜爱，但对Unobtanium不了解。
• TechnicJelle作为某应用的开发者，坦承该应用不如Obtainium，并说明因学习目的开发且暂无进一步开发计划。
• 0x073批评某应用的名称与其实际功能不符。
• Rocketvole询问Android平台上Unobtanium和Obtainium的区别，表现出对两者功能差异的困惑。
• Gitroom附和0xbadcafebee的观点，对移动设备锁定机制表示不满，并质疑这种做法背后的真正目的。
• Noname120指出某应用已有两年未更新，质疑其是否功能完备。
• FloatArtifact询问Windows平台上的类似工具，表现出对跨平台解决方案的兴趣。
• Interior推荐Unobtanium，认为Obtainium看起来并不在积极维护中。
• Dengolius提出F-Droid作为一个具有良好图形界面的替代方案，暗示其可能更适合用户需求。
• Yesbut简单支持F-Droid，未做详细说明。
• Sneak提到对微软远程代码执行（RCE）的担忧，暗示对依赖GitHub等平台的安全性问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是移动设备应用管理工具的必要性和现有工具的优劣，比如Unobtanium与Obtainium的功能对比。
• 另一个焦点是移动设备生态系统的封闭性和锁定机制，用户对此表达了不满，并讨论了这种机制对用户自由和设备寿命的影响。
• 安全性问题也被提及，特别是对依赖于某些平台的工具和应用的潜在安全风险的担忧。

总结：讨论围绕应用管理工具的功能、开发状态及其在不同平台上的替代方案展开，同时对移动设备生态系统的开放性和安全性提出了质疑。

43875476.article_content:
Yesterday, a Reuters photographer captured a
photo
of the freshly-ousted former National Security Advisor Mike Waltz checking his Signal messages during a Trump cabinet meeting. If you're not familiar with Waltz, he's most well known for inviting The Atlantic's editor-in-chief to secret Trump administration
war crimes Signal group
. They discussed, and executed, bombing an urban apartment building full of civilians to kill a single man.
404 Media journalist Joseph Cox
published a story
pointing out that Waltz was not using the official Signal app, but rather "an obscure and unofficial version of Signal that is designed to archive messages" called TM SGNL.
Zoomed-in crop of the Reuters photo showing Mike Waltz using the TM SGNL app. Images credit: REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein
This app uses Signal's servers, making it possible for Waltz to send end-to-end encrypted messages to normal Signal users, like Jeffrey Goldberg from The Atlantic, for example. However unlike the Signal end of the encrypted conversation, the TM SGNL end automatically archives a copy of the plaintext messages (even ones with disappearing messages) somewhere else that may or may not be secure.
In a
video
the company published, they show Signal messages getting archived into a Gmail account.
I decided to look into this app. I discovered:
The senior executives of the company behind TM SGNL appear to be Israeli, and the CEO's bio mentions his work with Israel Defense Forces' Intelligence unit.
TM SGNL is most likely violating Signal's open source license, and the company's other apps are probably violating the proprietary licenses of other software like WhatsApp and WeChat.
The Android and iOS versions of the app are not available for the public to download, and in fact practically the only way to get the app is if you're using a device enrolled in an MDM service that's tied to an Apple Business Manager or Google Enterprise account.
I speculate about exactly how I think the Trump administration is using this (unapproved for classified info) app to discuss classified info, and how they are likely managing their fleet of iPhones.
Finally, I share a PDF and a video I discovered that go into detail about, among other things, where the chat logs may be stored.
Before I get started, consider
subscribing
to get these posts emailed directly to your inbox. If you want to support my work, considering becoming a paid supporter.
The company behind TM SGNL
The TM SGNL app is part of a suite of apps by a company called
TeleMessage
, which is owned by
Smarsh
, a company that makes e-discovery software, which is basically software designed for police and lawyers and whatnot to search archives of data.
I haven't spent a lot of time looking into TeleMessage, but what I did find at a quick glance is that several of the executives on the
teams page
list Israeli universities in their bios, and the CEO, Guy Levit, says that, "From 1996 until 1999, Guy served as the head of the planning and development of one of the IDF’s Intelligence elite technical units."
How the app probably works
Based on the photo of Waltz's screen, TM SGNL is most likely a version of Signal that is slightly modified. The app name is changed from "Signal" to "TM SGNL" (which is why Walt'z screen says, "Verify your TM SGNL PIN" instead of "Verify your Signal PIN").
And there is most likely an additional piece of code that gets executed whenever a message is sent or received which forwards the plaintext version of that message to the "corporate archive," as the company calls it.
TM SGNL might be violating Signal's open source licenses
Signal is open source. Here's the
Signal-iOS
code and here's the
Signal-Android
code. Because the code is available, creating an app like TM SGNL would actually be pretty easy to do.
Signal has done all of the hard work in making an end-to-end encryption messaging app. Signal also runs the server infrastructure. The TeleMessage devs simply have to clone the git repos of the client apps, figure out where to insert the archiving code, and make their own separate releases.
The Signal apps are licensed under the
GNU Affero General Public License
, a copyleft license that allows anyone to make modified versions (like TM SGNL) provided that they also use the same open source license. The license text says that when making modifications to the source code:
You must license the entire work, as a whole, under this License to anyone who comes into possession of a copy.
So, if someone has a copy of TM SGNL, they should be able to request that TeleMessage provide a copy of the source code, which should also be open source, and if TeleMessage does not comply they will be violating Signal's license – essentially, selling pirated software.
TeleMessage also publishes similar apps for WhatsApp, Telegram, and even WeChat, that probably work in similar ways. But because these apps are proprietary, I can't see any way that they're

data.title: Connomore64: Cycle exact emulation of the C64 using parallel microcontrollers
data.author: codewiz
data.article_summary: Connomore64 是一个使用多个微控制器并行运行的Commodore 64（C64）计算机的实时循环精确仿真项目。该项目旨在通过廉价的RP2040/RP2350微控制器（每芯片不到1欧元）重建C64，通过8位多路复用总线以约8 MHz的有效速度互连，使用DVI/HDMI输出视频和音频，并精确模拟原始硬件信号时序。它可以与C1541软驱和一些扩展硬件接口，支持快速加载器。此外，它也是一个示例，展示了如何在廉价低功耗的互连微控制器上运行计算密集型软件，并作为调试和测试多个RP2040/RP2350并行项目的仿真框架。该项目起源于2022年圣诞节的业余项目，目标是探索RP2040微控制器的潜力，特别是其PIO（GPIO处理协处理器）。与现有简化版的C64仿真器不同，Connomore64追求精确的循环和时序仿真，同时兼容物理 retro 硬件。硬件方面，使用了自定义PCB（Breadbox v0原型），支持C64的常用端口和HDMI、音频输出。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕C64 SID芯片及相关硬件、仿真器项目的讨论，包括技术细节、实际应用以及怀旧情感。

不同观点：
• rollcat：对SID芯片声音的热爱，分享了与SID芯片相关的项目和艺术家链接。对实际项目和艺术创作的积极评价。
• bitwize：讨论了通过多个CPU分别仿真不同组件以实现精确时序仿真的技术想法，并对该想法的实现表示赞赏，但指出细节处理的复杂性。
• sandos：最初误以为该项目可以用来替换C64的损坏部件，但发现并非如此。表达了理解和接受。
• wiz21c：对图形渲染代码重写后速度提升但兼容性下降表示遗憾，质疑选择这种做法的原因。
• abhisek：虽然不热衷于硬件，但因为怀旧而尝试构建仿真器，分享了学习经历。

• chillingeffect：热爱修复C64，分享了自己的修复经验和成本，对使用Rpi pico替代CIA芯片的可能性表示好奇，并提出了技术细节问题。
