Spotlight on RSAC
91
The one interview question that will protect you from North Korean fake workers
91
FBI and others list how to spot NK infiltrators, but AI will make it harder
Iain Thomson
Tue 29 Apr 2025
//
09:15 UTC
RSAC
Concerned a new recruit might be a North Korean stooge out to steal intellectual property and then hit an org with malware? There is an answer, for the moment at least.
According to Adam Meyers, CrowdStrike's senior veep in the counter adversary division, North Korean infiltrators are bagging roles worldwide throughout the year. Thousands are said to have
infiltrated
the Fortune 500.
They're masking IPs, exporting laptop farms to America so they can connect into those machines and appear to be working from the USA, and they are using AI – but there's a question during job interviews that never fails to catch them out and forces them to drop out of the recruitment process.
"My favorite interview question, because we've interviewed quite a few of these folks, is something to the effect of 'How fat is Kim Jong Un?' They terminate the call instantly, because it's not worth it to say something negative about that," he
told
a panel session at the
RSA Conference
in San Francisco Monday.
Meyers explained the North Koreans will use generative AI to develop bulk batches of LinkedIn profiles and applications for remote work jobs that appeal to Western companies. During an interview, multiple teams will work on the technical challenges that are part of the interview while the "front man" handles the physical side of the interview, although sometimes rather ineptly.
"One of the things that we've noted is that you'll have a person in Poland applying with a very complicated name," he recounted, "and then when you get them on Zoom calls it's a military age male Asian who can't pronounce it." But it works enough that quite a few score the job and millions of dollars are being funneled back to North Korea via this route.
Once placed in the coveted role, such workers are usually very successful in the company, since they have multiple people working on one job to produce the best work possible - with the hope of getting a promotion and more access to the business' systems - explained panelist FBI Special Agent Elizabeth Pelker.
"I think more often than not, I get the comment of 'Oh, but Johnny is our best performer. Do we actually need to fire him?" she said.
The aims of
these phony workers
are two-fold, she explained. Firstly, they earn a wage and use their access to steal intellectual property from the victim. This is usually exfiltrated in tiny chunks so as to not trigger security systems.
One mitigation strategy, she said, was to insist that any interviewee performed coding tests within the corporate environment. These allow the actual IP being used to get checked, interviewers to see how often the prospect is switching between screens, and can allow other clues to leak out that all is not as it seems.
If the interloper is exposed and fired, however, they will usually have already collected login details, planted unactivated malware, and will then attempt to extort the maximum they can from the victim. She urged anyone who spots a fake employee to contact their local FBI field office immediately.
The Red Queen's race
But the attackers are getting smarter, and in some ways the FBI is a victim of its own success.
The agency has been distributing
advice
to US companies but these memos are also being read in Pyongyang and the workers are adapting their tactics. This sometimes involves using both aware and unwitting accomplices.
For example, to get around the IP address problem, laptop farms are springing up all over America. If an applicant gets a job, the firm will usually send him a laptop, at which point the interviewee explains that they've moved or have a family emergency, so could they send it to a new address please?

I'm a security expert, and I almost fell for a North Korea-style deepfake job applicant …Twice

busted

data.author: ano-ther

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容对人际交流和书面沟通的影响

不同观点：
• **AI使交流失去个人温度和真实性**：[sepositus] 提到他的孩子用AI写感谢信，虽然形式上完成了任务，但缺乏个人情感，显得冷漠和不真诚。他担心未来人们会不再重视人与人之间的交流温度。
   
• **AI生成内容的正确性和语气问题**：[ash_091] 认为，使用AI辅助写作本身没问题，但直接发送未经审核的AI生成内容可能导致语气和准确性问题，令人担忧。

• **AI可能被用来伪造和削弱真实性**：[Terr_] 引用了“伪造”和“贬值”等词汇，指出AI可能被用来伪造表面信号，使人们难以判断内容的真实性和作者的实际能力。

• **个人不完美写作的可接受性**：[neom] 认为，由于自身阅读障碍，他们不太在意写作的完美性，反而觉得AI能帮助那些因不自信而拖延的人更快完成任务。

• **对AI生成内容的厌倦**：[agentultra] 表示，如果人们连自己写邮件的功夫都不愿意花，那他们的信息根本不值得读。

• **AI对社会的多重影响**：[A4ET8a8uTh0_v2] 探讨了AI对社会多方面的影响，包括AI在网络流量中的作用和AI验证人类性项目的兴起。

• **AI生成内容的质量问题**：[analog31] 认为，即使没有AI，大多数人的写作本来就不值得一读，AI生成内容如果基于大量平庸的人类文本，质量也不会高。

• **AI自动交流的未来**：[michaeljx] 开玩笑地提议让两个AI直接互发邮件，省去人类参与的必要。

• **保持自然写作的重要性**：[satisfice] 认为，人们将不再信任任何使用AI写作的人，除非他们建立了自然写作的声誉。

• **AI在个人和商业关系中的有限应用**：[rorylaitila] 强调，他只会在邮件中使用简单的自动完成功能，并明确表示不愿意生活在一个充满AI对话的世界中。

• **AI助长懒惰**：[miragecraft] 认为，人们过度依赖AI来完成任务，而不是用它来提升自己。

• **对AI的适应过程**：[dotslashmain] 认为，人们会对AI的使用逐渐习以为常，最初的过度思考会随时间消散。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI生成内容是否会削弱人际交流的真实性和温度，以及人们如何适应和规范AI在书面沟通中的使用。
• 一些评论者担心AI生成内容的质量和准确性，而另一些则认为AI可以帮助那些有写作困难的人，提高效率。
• 讨论中还涉及到AI对社会多方面的潜在影响，包括个人隐私和人类验证项目等。

data.title: RethinkDNS Resolver That Deploys to CF Workers, Deno Deploy, Fastly, Fly.io
data.author: indigodaddy
data.article_summary: **serverless-dns** 是一个自托管的、类似Pi-Hole的内容拦截DNS解析器，支持DNS-over-HTTPS（DoH）和DNS-over-TLS（DoT）。它可以无服务器方式部署在Cloudflare Workers、Deno Deploy、Fastly Compute@Edge和Fly.io平台上，免费 tier 足够支持10到20台设备的DNS流量。RethinkDNS在多个云平台上运行，响应时间在0到2毫秒之间，端到端延迟为10到30毫秒。用户可以通过简单配置自定义拦截列表，并在不同平台上进行设置。代码遵循Google JavaScript风格指南，并通过pre-commit钩子确保代码质量。支持使用字母数字承载令牌进行DoH和DoT的身份验证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rethink DNS的性能、技术实现及其现状

不同观点：
• [maxloh的观点] 对Rethink DNS服务器使用JavaScript实现表示怀疑，认为JavaScript作为性能关键的DNS服务器语言可能较慢。通过基准测试显示，Rethink DNS处理DNS请求需要400-500ms，而Cloudflare仅需5-10ms。基于性能考虑，最终选择了AdAway。

• [chrisweekly的观点] 对Rethink DNS表示认可，提到它类似于Pi-hole，并顺带提到Bunny.net作为其新的CDN/云服务提供商，暗示对Rethink DNS的积极态度，特别是其DNS可编程性。

• [Onavo的观点] 对Rethink DNS移动应用多年未发布新版本表示担忧，质疑该项目是否仍然活跃，并提供了GitHub链接以供参考。

补充讨论：
• 性能是主要争议焦点，尤其是JavaScript在处理DNS请求时的速度问题。
• maxloh提供了具体的测试数据来支持其观点，强调性能对比。
• chrisweekly更关注Rethink DNS的功能和类似工具，对性能问题未做深入讨论。
• Onavo关心项目的活跃性和持续性，提出了对Rethink DNS未来发展的疑问。

data.title: Show HN: Free, in-browser PDF editor
data.author: philjohnson
data.article_summary: Breeze PDF是一款强大且免费的PDF编辑工具，完全在浏览器中离线运行，确保100%隐私。用户无需上传文件，所有处理都在本地进行，保障文件安全。它支持添加文本、图片、签名、表单域，还能合并、删除页面以及为PDF加密。该工具无需安装，适用于任何现代浏览器，并可在离线状态下使用。Breeze PDF承诺不将文件上传至服务器，确保用户对敏感信息的控制和保密。该工具免费无限制，适合桌面使用，移动端也可访问但体验可能受屏幕尺寸影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PDF编辑工具的功能、使用体验、技术实现及隐私问题

不同观点：
• 一些用户对工具的实用性表示赞赏，并提到会在特定场景下使用，如[throwanem]和[contact9879]。他们表示会将该工具加入书签以备后用。
• [speerer]对工具的技术实现提出建议，推荐使用MuPDF的WASM编译版本，并询问了关于选择特定pdf-lib分支的原因。
• [kevinlinxc]和[tbarbe]推荐了其他类似的PDF工具，如stirling-pdf和pdfModer，强调了本地运行和开源的优势。
• [nestorD]提出了对扫描版PDF处理的需求，如分割页面、清理文本和压缩等功能，并推荐了Xournal++作为替代方案。
• [cbracketdash]对用户界面和用户体验提出了详细的意见，包括滚动问题、模态框关闭方式、文本编辑功能不足等。

补充讨论：
• [jbarrow]提到其AI工具在PDF中自动添加表单字段的难度，并认可该工具的表单处理能力。
• [nizarmah]提出小请求防止误关标签页，以及大请求图片和签名调整功能。
• [behnamoh]指出工具仅能添加文本而不能编辑现有文本的问题。
• [lutusp]从根本上质疑PDF编辑工具的必要性，认为PDF应保持其原始只读目的。
• [kzrdude]指出下载PDF时文本块换行不一致的问题。
• [jdjdjdjdjd]和[cbracketdash]都提到无法滚动查看PDF的问题。
• [Labo333]寻求PDF审查工具或Python库，以实现对内容的去除而不仅仅是遮盖。
• [VisualByte]对工具的隐私保护表示不信任，要求查看其代码仓库。

争议焦点：
• PDF编辑工具的用户体验和功能实现存在一定争议，尤其是文本编辑、界面操作和用户需求满足方面。
• 对工具隐私保护的信任问题也被提出，反映了用户对在线工具安全性的关注。

data.title: We fell out of love with Next.js and back in love with Ruby on Rails
data.author: mike1o1
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Hardcover团队从Next.js迁移回Ruby on Rails与Inertia.js的经历。最初，团队因Next.js的SEO能力和服务端渲染（SSR）优势选择了它，但随着应用增长，客户端数据获取导致性能下降和API服务器压力增大。尽管尝试使用Next.js的App Router和React Server Components来改善，问题仍未完全解决。最终，团队决定回归更熟悉的Ruby on Rails，结合Inertia.js，实现了更高效的开发和性能优化。这一转变显著提升了应用的速度和稳定性，使团队重拾对Rails的热爱。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于服务器端渲染（SSR）、全栈JavaScript开发、框架选择及复杂性管理的讨论

不同观点：
• **服务器端渲染的回归**：thembones认为服务器端渲染从未真正消失，目前由于首屏渲染速度和SEO的优势，正在重新受到重视。多个框架如Rails + Turbo、HTMX、Phoenix LiveView和React Server Components都将SSR作为默认选项。现代趋势是“默认使用HTML，只在必要时加入JavaScript”，以减少复杂性和安全风险。

• **全栈JavaScript开发的挑战**：madethemcry指出全栈JavaScript开发（包括数据库操作）面临许多选择问题，如ORM碎片化或纯SQL编写。虽然个人项目可能选择Ruby on Rails更愉快，但由于Rails开发者稀缺，专业项目中不切实际。多数人仍会选择JavaScript或Java作为后端技术。

• **技术栈的实际价值**：austin-cheney质疑许多关于技术栈的讨论，认为其核心目标仅仅是“将文本展示在屏幕上”，并质疑这些复杂技术栈是否真正节省时间与成本，指出很少有开发者能给出具体数值。

• **Rails的优劣**：bckr对Rails的好处有所耳闻，但想知道除了学习新语言和框架之外的缺点。mountainriver则表示对Rails没有特别感受，更倾向于使用Go或Rust来编写可扩展的服务器。

• **Next.js与其他SSR方案的比较**：littlecranky67认为Next.js作为混合框架表现出色，质疑为何要争论Next.js与SSR的对比，并希望看到实际性能指标对比。swyx提到Next.js的托管费用增长问题，指出微小决策可能导致巨大成本影响。

• **框架选择的实践经验**：ww520分享了使用Spring Boot和Solid.js的成功项目经验，指出这种组合高效且稳定，但需要自行解决多数据库系统连接问题。

• **前端框架的自由选择**：hijp认为如果Rails支持更多前端框架的原生集成（如React），会更受欢迎。dzonga则支持Inertia.js，认为它避免了Hotwire的混乱，允许选择自己熟悉的前端框架。

• **安全与框架选择的顾虑**：ronbenton对同构框架（isomorphic frameworks）趋势感到担忧，担心出现服务器端代码或数据意外泄露到客户端的安全问题。

• **Inertia.js与SSG的复杂性**：joshstrange对Inertia.js的“魔法”感到不安，认为JS生态系统不稳定，SSG（静态站点生成）虽然有价值但增加了复杂性，不确定是否可离线使用。

补充讨论：
• **Rails与其他语言框架的结合**：omneity分享了从Rails迁移到Node.js后再部分回迁的经历，认为将“行政部分”放在Rails中，而“业务服务”留在JS或Python中是最佳实践。

• **技术栈趋势的反思**：rustc询问是否有具备强静态类型系统的Rails替代品。DuzAwe则隐晦地表示技术可能在“向后滚动”，暗示AI可能无法支持最新的技术趋势。

争议焦点：
• **服务器端渲染与客户端渲染的优劣对比**：关于SSR与SPA/SSG的实际性能与复杂性管理存在争议，部分人认为现代SPA框架如Next.js已很好地平衡了渲染性能与开发体验，而另一部分人则认为HTML和SSR才是减少复杂性的正确方向。

• **Rails的适用性**：关于Rails是否适合现代开发需求存在分歧，部分人认为Rails在个人项目中体验良好，但缺乏专业项目中的可行性，而其他人则倾向于使用如Go、Rust等更具扩展性的语言。

43881035.article_content:
Part 1: How We Fell Out of Love with Next.js and Back in Love with Ruby on Rails & Inertia.js
Adam Fortuna
By
Adam Fortuna
Fri, 02 May 2025 00:00:00 +0000
·
20
min read
This is
part 1
of a series documenting
Hardcover’s Alexandria release
. We recently migrated our codebase from Next.js to Ruby on Rails, and it’s been amazing so far! It was a learning experience, and I’m excited to share some of our takeaways. I’ll link each article here as it’s written.
Introducing Alexandria: Faster, Smoother, Smarter
Part 1: How we fell out of love with Next.js and back in love with Ruby on Rails & Inertia.js
Part 2: Moving from the Cloud to the Server – Google & AWS to Digital Ocean and Kamal
Part 3: How we use Puppeteer to generate OpenGraph images
Part 4: Speeding up Ruby on Rails with Solid Cache, server side rendering, Sidekiq, and Brick
Part 5: Securing and Speeding up our API Server
Today’s focus is on the main reason for the move from Next.js to Ruby on Rails. This is the first question anyone asks, and the most important one. So let’s dive into it.
Just a side note: this is going to be a software development related post, not a book related posts. If you’re here for the Book Vibes, I’d encourage you read about the
release first
.
How We Got Here
When Hardcover started, I was primarily a Ruby on Rails developer. I had experience with JS frontends, but Rails was my
jam
. I’ve been building things in it since before Rails 1.0, worked at multiple startups that use it, built courses to teach it, spoken at meetups about it, and been to conferences.
I’ve been
all in
with Rails for a while.
In the late 2010s, single page applications broke out as an alternative way to create applications. It was the JavaScript framework Cambrian Explosion – with jQuery as the common ancestor (in spirit at least).
We had Backbone.js, Ember.js, Angular.js, Vue.js, React.js and many more. I’ve shipped code in each of these frameworks that have been seen by millions people (which is easier than it sounds! I’ve heard you can just
do stuff
– especially on the Internet).
The biggest point of friction with these frameworks was always how they would integrate with Ruby on Rails. Rails has gone down a different route for it’s sanctioned front-end path – using
Islands Architecture
, Stimulus Controllers and other solutions (which are all preferred to Rails previous .rjs syntax).
I’ll be honest: I haven’t spent the time to fully learn this architecture. I can’t criticize it, other than that the code looks
weird
to me. It does have advantages over JS frameworks, but you’re still writing JS either way.
For most of the past decade, using these popular frameworks in Rails has meant giving up
Server Side Rendering
. In 2021 when I started Hardcover, that one fact alone meant it was out. We knew we’d need to rely on SEO to find new readers and I didn’t want to sacrifice that.
Enter Next.js
Right as I was deciding on what framework to use that would allow for SEO + JavaScript, Next.js announced version 9.5  – adding incremental static regeneration and other features that would allow us to render pages with SSR and expire the cache. It sounded perfect.
I setup the initial architecture of Hardcover using Next.js with the pages router, hitting a GraphQL API (Hasura) for getting data, and caching as much as possible using Incremental Static Revalidation. The first load was often a bit slow, but caching helped.
One decision I made during this phase would come back to haunt me:
cache facts on the server, fetch user data in the browser
.
For instance, if you’re viewing a Readers profile,
everything
we show there would be fetched client-side from our GraphQL API. Our API returns different results depending on your relationship with the reader you’re viewing. Someone can mark a book, list or goal as public, private or only people you follow – which all determine what other readers can see.
This approach left that logic to the API, allowing the front-end to be dumb and just show whatever was returned. It
worked
.
Behind the scenes we were still using Ruby on Rails for the entire backend. This is what the architecture looked like at the time.
From 2021 to 2022 we continued on building like this. Some pages were getting slower, but we were able to ship fast. We continued innovating, but the app kept getting slower. As more readers joined, we were hitting our API servers
hard
, and we couldn’t cache anything at that level. If we wanted server side caching, we needed to move that to the server.
An Wild App Router Appears
In mid-2022, Next.js launched the App Router – a new way to server side render Next.js apps. I loved the idea. It felt more like Rails which I was used to. We immediately starting migrating Hardcover to this approach.
We switched to fetching all data about facts and users to be fetched on the server using the app directory and React Server Components. This went surprisingly smooth! There were some rough days with next-auth and Apollo to get everything
43881035.article_summary: 本文介绍了Hardcover团队从Next.js迁移回Ruby on Rails与Inertia.js的经历。最初，团队因Next.js的SEO能力和服务端渲染（SSR）优势选择了它，但随着应用增长，客户端数据获取导致性能下降和API服务器压力增大。尽管尝试使用Next.js的App Router和React Server Components来改善，问题仍未完全解决。最终，团队决定回归更熟悉的Ruby on Rails，结合Inertia.js，实现了更高效的开发和性能优化。这一转变显著提升了应用的速度和稳定性，使团队重拾对Rails的热爱。

data.title: DuckDB is probably the most important geospatial software of the last decade
data.author: dbreunig
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了DuckDB在地理空间数据处理方面的重要性，尤其是在其发布空间扩展后，显著降低了处理地理空间数据的难度。过去，处理这些数据需要安装多个开源软件包、配置路径以及搭建专用数据库，而现在通过DuckDB，只需一两行代码即可实现。这大大简化了操作，吸引了更多非专业人士参与地理空间数据工作，扩大了该领域的影响力。文章还提到，在Cloud-Native Geospatial会议上，DuckDB的空间扩展被视为扩大地理空间数据受众的关键工具，可能推动了Overture Maps Foundation等项目的使用增长。作者对DuckDB在这一领域的未来发展表示期待。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DuckDB在地理空间分析中的作用和独特性

不同观点：
• Demiurge认为，DuckDB并没有显著简化安装和设置过程，因为像PostGIS这样的工具已经存在多年，且功能类似。DuckDB并没有在易用性上带来实质性的改变。
• Wenc赞赏DuckDB能够在本地桌面处理大规模的parquet/geoparquet文件，并通过向量化与并行化提升工作效率。DuckDB支持如Hilbert曲线和Uber H3等高级地理空间功能，提供了质量上的改进。
• Larsiusprime质疑DuckDB的独特性，指出"import geopandas"也存在，并希望看到更实际的例子来说明DuckDB的特别之处。
• Jparishy更关注Felt.com，认为其在地理空间技术与消费者应用集成方面有潜力，并提到培训人们掌握坐标系统、投影、转换等技能的难度。
• Wodenokoto和WD-42都认为DuckDB在安装简便性上并不比"pip install geopandas"或"docker pull postgis"有显著优势。
• Feverzsj指出DuckDB在处理大量空间索引查询时速度较慢，因为其使用列式存储。
• Patja提到SQL Server多年前就提供了无需扩展的地理空间功能，且免费的Express版本就足够使用。
• Twelvechairs认为DuckDB并非过去十年中最重要的地理空间工具，列举了QGIS、PostGIS、ArcGIS、Mapbox等其他重要工具。
• Badmonster提出DuckDB将地理空间能力嵌入通用数据工具可能会改变参与地理空间分析的人员构成及其解决问题的方式。
• WD-42还提到DuckDB使用的许可证可能导致类似Redis的法律问题。
• Fidotron认为Uber的H3系统可能更值得关注。
• Jandrewrogers认为地理空间软件长期停滞不前，新工具只是旧工具的新包装，并建议地理空间软件应摆脱制图学的束缚。
• Bingaweek和Cyanydeez都对标题中对DuckDB的高度评价表示不屑，认为QGIS才是最重要的工具。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的工具和技术包括PostGIS、MySQL、Oracle、MS SQL Server、SQLite、DuckDB、geopandas、Felt.com、QGIS、ArcGIS、Mapbox、deckgl、COG、geoparquet、gdal、pdal、shapely、H3等。
• 许可证问题和软件的法律风险也被提及，特别是与Redis许可证类似的潜在问题。
• 争议的焦点在于DuckDB是否真正带来了显著的改进和独特性，以及其在地理空间分析领域的重要性。

43881468.article_content:
May 3, 2025
GEO
DUCKDB
UX
DuckDB is Probably the Most Important Geospatial Software of the Last Decade
What happens when you embed geospatial capabilities in generalist data tools? More people engaging with geo data.
I just returned from the inaugural
Cloud-Native Geospatial conference
. It was fantastic, I highly recommend you jump in if Jed and team organized another.
One of the core questions discussed in the breakouts and in the halls was how to broaden the geospatial audience. How can we better communicate geo data’s utility, in all industries and domains? Many tactics and case studies were debated, but the one I kept coming back to is that of DuckDB.
This chart could’ve been pretty bleak! Interest in “geospatial” (a term that functions well as a proxy for similar terms) declined and flatlined until late 2023 – right when DuckDB released their
spatial extension
.
Now, all the standard caveats about correlation and causation apply, but I’m inclined to believe this chart.
DuckDB lowers the barriers to working with geo data to
two lines
:
install
spatial
;
load
spatial
;
If the extension is already installed, it’s only
one
line.
Prior to this, getting up and running from a cold-start might’ve required installing or even compiling severall OSS packages, carefully noting path locations, standing up a specialized database… Enough work that a data generalist might not have bothered, or their IT department might not have supported it.
With DuckDB spatial, it became possible for casual geospatial work to occur. All within SQL… And that makes the ecosystem bigger.
As I discussed the spatial extension and this chart between sessions at the Cloud Native Geospatial conference, I wondered: would
Overture Maps Foundation
have the usage it has today without DuckDB spatial? Maybe…but probably not.
I’m excited to help those spikes at the end of the chart continue upward.
Enter your email to receive the occasional update.

data.title: Lessons from Building a Translator App That Beats Google Translate and DeepL
data.author: msephton
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了作者开发的一款名为Kintoun的翻译应用，该应用在许多情况下比Google Translate和DeepL表现更好。作者通过实际文档翻译对比，展示了Kintoun在保持原文布局和翻译准确性上的优势。文章分享了三个主要经验：

1. **产品质量意外超越大公司**：尽管作者自认编程水平一般，且仅用业余时间开发，Kintoun在处理文档翻译和布局保持上优于Google Translate和DeepL。

2. **产品分发与开发同等重要**：作者意识到推广和分发产品与开发产品同样关键。建议先找到已经寻找解决方案的用户，再进行产品推介，而不是盲目开发。

3. **技术选择至关重要**：作者在技术框架选择上，发现Inertia.js和Svelte的组合极大地简化了开发过程，提升了应用的响应性。

作者强调，在产品开发前应考虑清楚分发策略，甚至可以先获取客户再进行开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于翻译应用的开发、优化及其市场前景的讨论

不同观点：
• [omneity] 开发了一个支持非传统语言对（如摩洛哥阿拉伯语）的翻译应用，并训练了一个自定义的翻译模型（BART变种），建立了持续训练管道。对低资源语言的翻译模型开发感兴趣的人可以参考Marian-NMT和Opus & Tatoeba项目。
• [kyrra] 认为Google Translate在速度和计算优化上有优势，模型大小仅约20mb，可以在手机上离线运行。虽然Gemini可能翻译效果更好，但Google的优化使其能够免费翻译网页。
• [DiscourseFan] 怀疑该应用是否为GPT的包装，并指出GPT是通用翻译工具，尽管其微调用途与上述应用不同。
• [whycome] 指出Google Translate有时只提供一个翻译选项，而实际上有多个可能的定义，特别是在对翻译语言有一定了解时更容易发现这些问题。

43839145.article_content:
Lessons From Building a Translator App That Beats Google Translate and DeepL
26 Apr 2025
How It Started
Recently, I made a new app called
Kintoun
. It’s a document translator that delivers very high quality translations and keeps the original layout almost perfectly.
At first, I didn’t expect much. But after comparing it with Google Translate and DeepL, I was surprised to see that my app actually performs better in many cases.
In this post, I want to share what I’ve learned while building it. Writing helps me organize my thoughts, and maybe some of this will be useful if you’re working on your own project too.
Lesson #1. Surprise: My app is actually better than Google Translate and DeepL
Let me show you some examples.
Document #1: Original
This is a Word document from
Microsoft
:
Download this file (docx)
Document #1: Google Translate Result
I translated it into Japanese using Google Translate:
Download this file (docx)
Google Translate couldn’t handle it well. The text wasn’t translated, and the layout and fonts got messed up. I tried with different documents and languages, and it was always the same.
Document #1: DeepL Result
Now let’s try DeepL:
Download this file (docx)
DeepL did a much better job, but some parts, like “Appetizer,” were missing.
Document #1: Kintoun Result
Finally, here is the result from Kintoun:
Download the file (docx)
.
Kintoun correctly translated all the text and kept the layout intact.
Document #2: Original
Sometimes documents have
Phonetic Guide Text
(also called Ruby text) to show pronunciation.
For example, Japanese documents often include Hiragana above Kanji.
Here is another document with phonetic guides:
Download the file (docx)
Document #2: Google Translate Result
I translated it into Japanese using Google Translate:
Download the file (docx)
Google Translate completely ignored the text with phonetic guides. The translation became incomplete and confusing.
Document #2: DeepL Result
Here is the result from DeepL:
Download the file (docx)
DeepL could handle the phonetic guides, but it broke the layout. For example, the bullet points in the table disappeared.
Document #2: Kintoun Result
And here is the result from Kintoun:
Download the file (docx)
Kintoun properly translated everything and preserved the layout.
I could show more examples, but you probably get the idea.
Honestly, it feels a bit surreal.
I’m just a bad amateur programmer who would fail any serious technical interview, and I only spent about two weeks of spare time, besides my day job and taking care of my kid.
How could I ever make something better than those big companies?
And yet, somehow, I did.
Lesson #2. Product distribution is as important as product development
I came across a
Reddit post
the other day, and it really hit me:
The pattern was always the same:
Get excited about an idea
Spend months building it
Launch to complete silence
Get depressed
Repeat
This is exactly me, and probably many other indie hackers.
The post also shared how to break the cycle:
What Worked:
Finding people ALREADY looking for a solution
Instead of cold DMs, I searched for posts like "anyone know a tool that..." or "frustrated with [competitor]" and offered genuine help.
Leading with help, not sales. My first message is usually answering their question thoroughly. Only AFTER providing value did I mention "I actually built a tool that might help..."
I read it carefully and have been keeping it in mind ever since. I also found the same advice from
Dmytro Krasun
, the maker of
screenshotone.com
:
If you don’t have any idea whom you are going to sell your product, don’t build it.
In practice, though, I didn’t really understand it until I released
Kintoun
and started promoting it. Right now, I only have some vague ideas about promotion. I don’t know which ones will work, or how exactly to execute them.
Looking back, I think I should have spent as much time figuring this out as I did building the app. Maybe even before starting development.
Or maybe I shouldn’t have built it at all until I had a clear idea about distribution, like the old “correct” way of bootstrapping: get customers first, then build (“fake it until you make it”).
Lesson #3. Inertia + Svelte is awesome
Maybe it’s just me being too dumb, but even after using
Hotwire
in production for a while, I could never really understand how it works.
For example:
How am I supposed to redirect the page with a 302?
How can I make five elements scattered across the page reactive without manually managing their IDs?
How should I submit a form correctly? Should I use Turbo Stream, Turbo Frame, or both?
Of course, I could go back to jQuery and the good old Asset Pipeline.
Actually, I’m still using that combination in production for work and side projects.
But it would be a nightmare if I ever wanted to make the app even slightly reactive.
After evaluating a bunch of options, I eventually landed on
Inertia.js
and
Svelte
.
The result was a complete game changer.
It became so easy and magi

data.title: Ghosts and Dolls
data.author: lermontov
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了由保罗·J·格里菲斯（Paul J. Griffiths）撰写的关于人工智能写作的文章。他通过19世纪英国女性作家使用男性笔名发表作品的现象，探讨了对写作者的偏见问题。这些作家使用男性 pseudonyms 是为了避免因性别偏见而遭到轻视，类似于当今人们对由大型语言生成人工智能创作的文学作品所持的偏见。有人认为人工智能的写作因其来源而受到“污染”，这种态度与过去对女性作家的歧视类似。尽管人工智能通过人类编写的代码和提示生成文本，但其创作过程并不完全受控于人类，这使得它们的创作行为与人类写作有相似之处。文章强调，“写作”指的是将词语排列成可读文本的行为，而不涉及作者是否有意识或思想。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对AI生成内容及其与人类创作的比较和争议

不同观点：
• jtwoodhouse认为将AI写作与女性写作相提并论是一种错误的等价，并且贬低了女性。他强调人类，特别是女性，通过痛苦和努力进行创作，而AI没有感觉和生命，只是重复已有的知识。他质疑为什么人们要关注AI生成的内容，而不是人类用心创作的作品。
• kmeisthax批评了为AI“艺术”辩护的文章，认为AI作为一种技术是反人本主义的。他指出AI依赖于未经同意获取的训练数据，其学习方式与人类截然不同。他还提到AI无法具有人性，因为它本质上是一个被操控的工具，无法脱离其创造者的控制。

补充讨论：
• jtwoodhouse通过个人情感和家庭关系的例子（如母亲的手写笔记）强调人类创作的独特价值，认为AI生成的内容缺乏这种情感深度和个人投入。
• kmeisthax更关注AI对艺术经济学的破坏，指出AI的大规模生产和精细调整使其成为一种工具，而不是具有创造力的个体。他还提到了AI可能带来的社会和伦理问题，例如通过操控实现特定目标的潜在危险。
• 争议的焦点在于AI生成内容是否可以与人类创作相提并论，以及AI对社会、经济和伦理的潜在影响。jtwoodhouse从情感和人类经验的角度出发，而kmeisthax则从技术、经济和人本主义的角度进行分析。

总结：评论主要围绕AI生成内容与人类创作的比较展开，涉及情感价值、技术特性、经济影响和社会伦理等多方面讨论。不同评论者从各自的角度出发，提出了对AI技术及其应用的深刻质疑。

Lent 2025
|
February 14, 2025
Features
Ghosts and Dolls
by
Paul J. Griffiths
On the writings of artificial intelligence.
About the author
by
Paul J. Griffiths
Paul J. Griffiths is a writer and theologian whose most recent book is
Israel: A Christian Grammar
(Fortress Press, 2023).
Read More
More By This Contributor
Against Human Flourishing
On a dualistic mode of thought.
The Lamp Magazine
Ghosts and Dolls
by
Paul J. Griffiths
Sometimes, for some people, a piece of writing’s attribution alone suffices to taint or burnish it. The attribution might be to this or that individual writer, or to one or another kind of writer. Those who take a piece of writing to be tainted in this way need no acquaintance with what it contains to support their judgement; attribution suffices.
It wasn’t, for example, uncommon in nineteenth-century England for female writers to publish under male pseudonyms. The Brontë sisters each did that when they began to publish, as did Mary Ann Evans, who is still mostly known as George Eliot. They did it principally because they and their publishers judged that under a female name their works would attract fewer readers; they would be read, if at all, read differently, with condescension or ridicule. Masculine pseudonymity in this case was a protective strategy. Those who used it wanted attention paid not to their persons in a kind but to what they’d written.
What the Brontës and Evans tried to protect themselves against is strictly a prejudice, a prejudgement, in the sense that it isn’t based upon acquaintance with what members of the kind in question have written. Rather, those who adopt it know, or take themselves to know, something about members of the kind that taints whatever they write. Perhaps it is that such writers are incapable of writing anything interesting; perhaps that they’re so heavily implicated in a noxious political or economic or cultural system that reading them serves to endorse something that shouldn’t be endorsed; perhaps that all writers of the kind are corrupt, maleficent, and dangerous, and therefore not to be consorted with by reading them; perhaps that they’re taking good work away from writers who belong to some other, more deserving kind, and therefore shouldn’t  be supported by readers. And so on.
A version of this attitude is at the moment widespread with respect to the literary writing done by large-language generative artificial intelligences. Some take such writing to be tainted just because it’s been done by such entities, without respect to its substance. The analogy with the judgement that women’s writing is tainted just because it’s done by women is formally exact.
A first objection to this analogy might say that what makes the difference between the case of women versus men and that of artificial versus human intelligence is not that the artificial intelligences compose differently than human beings do but that they do not compose at all, which is manifestly not so for women. That is so because the procedures that produce the texts that artificial intelligences seem to compose are run by human-written code and initiated by human-provided prompts. Artificial intelligences execute commands as puppets do; that is the extent of their action, and it is this state of affairs that, while not exactly tainting the texts they seem to compose, makes it improper to say that they have composed them at all. On this view, machines do not write; at best they copy.
This line of response is inadequate to the ways in which coders and computer scientists describe what large-language generative artificial intelligences do. It is by now commonplace to say that these can and do themselves write (the preferred verb in the trade) and compile code that runs routines, and that what they do in response to human requests is neither predictable by nor transparent to those who wrote and compiled the code that brought them into being and established the parameters of their activity. These features of their performance are among the principal reasons for current anxiety about them; they show artificial intelligences of this type to be significantly unlike puppets. They also make them significantly like, in their compositional use of language, human persons. We too have been given language, spoken and written, by others than ourselves; we too compose in response to stimuli that come to us from without; and we too compose according to grammatical rules we did not make and in response to already extant texts composed by others.
“Writing” is here shorthand for composition, which is the act of putting words in order so as to bring into being a legible verbal ensemble. Such ensembles are texts, or pieces of writing. No claim is made or denied by the use of the word about the mindedness or thoughtfulness or meaningfulness of the act by which the words of a text are ordered, or about the nature and origin of those who do it; the only claim the word makes, as used here, is about the legibili

data.author: goranmoomin
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了作者在使用MathML渲染方程时遇到的挑战，以及最终选择Pandoc作为解决方案的经历。作者起初尝试多种工具和库，但都不尽如人意，甚至手写MathML。后来发现Pandoc不仅能有效处理单个方程，还能轻松应对多行方程和矩阵。然而，Pandoc在转换某些复杂公式（如包含求和和极限的公式）时存在一个小错误，即极限符号的格式不正确。作者分析了MathML输出，找到了问题所在，但因不会编程，决定向Pandoc的开发者反馈此问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Pandoc及其在数学公式转换中的应用和相关技术选择

不同观点：
• fiddlosopher（Pandoc开发者）指出Pandoc使用texmath库来转换方程，并提供了生成独立可执行文件和web服务器的方法。他还解释了关于空`<mo></mo>`的误解，指出其中包含不可见的U+2061字符，并计划通过将`<mi>`和`<mo>`放入`<mrow>`来解决问题。

• seanhunter认为作者所提到的问题并非Pandoc的bug，而是由于LaTeX书写不明确所致。他认为如果希望限制符号总是显示在下面，应该使用`\lim\limits_{n \to \infty}`的写法，这同样适用于求和和积分符号。

• satgo1546支持在Markdown源代码中保留MathML而不是LaTeX，并提到自己编写了一个AutoHotkey脚本用于Markdown到HTML的转换。他还考虑使用Pandoc来替代当前的cmark后端以支持MathML。

• bArray分享了其在2021年遇到的MathML在Chrome等浏览器中支持不佳的问题，并最终选择了Preet的一个小实现方案，同时对未来转换到SVG矢量格式表达了兴趣。他还提到对当前解决方案中复杂的LaTeX包装器的不满，并考虑编写一个转换MathML的解析器。

• ayhanfuat提到GitHub最近也开始使用MathML，认为这是一个不错的回归。

• huijzer询问是否有其他类似的转换工具，表示虽然喜欢Pandoc，但在生产环境中运行时遇到了一些不满意的地方，但未具体说明原因。

补充讨论：
• 关于MathML在不同浏览器中的支持情况及其替代方案（如SVG矢量格式）的讨论。
• Pandoc在实际应用中的一些技术选择和生产环境中的挑战。
• 不同用户在处理数学公式转换时采用的自定义脚本和工具，如AutoHotkey和Pandoc。

43880554.article_content:
And now it’s all this I just said what I said and it was wrong Or was taken wrong Previous post MathML with Pandoc May 3, 2025 at 11:25 AM by Dr. Drang Since switching from MathJax to MathML to render equations here on ANIAT, I’ve tried several approaches to generate the MathML. There are many utilities and libraries that claim to do the conversion, but I’ve found all of them to be limited in one way or another. For a while, I was even writing MathML directly, albeit with the help of some Typinator abbreviations, because I couldn’t trust the converters to generate the correct characters or even understand some LaTeX commands I use regularly. Recently, I began using what I should have started out with: Pandoc . It’s not that I wasn’t aware of Pandoc. Its famous in the Markdown/HTML/LaTeX world, and I probably first heard of it shortly after its release. But I’ve always thought of it as a document converter, not an equation converter. I was wrong. It’s very easy to use with a single equation. pandoc --mathml <<<'$$T = \frac{1}{2} v_x^2$$' produces

T = 12 vx2 T = \frac{1}{2} v_x^2

where I’ve added linebreaks and indentation to the output to make it easier to read. Because it’s delimited by double dollar signs, the equation is rendered in block mode, like this: T = 1 2 v 2 Single dollar signs would generate MathML with a display="inline" attribute. (If you look at the source code for this page, you’ll see that I usually delete some of the code Pandoc generates—we’ll get to that later.) All the converters handled simple equations, like v 0 2 , well, but more complicated stuff can be troublesome. One of the problems other converters have is dealing with multiline equations, something Pandoc handles with ease. For example, this piecewise function definition, $$ f(x) = \left\{ \begin{array} {rcl} -1 & : & x<0 \\ 0 & : & x=0 \\ +1 & : & x>0 \end{array} $$ is rendered exactly as expected: f ( x ) = { − 1 : x < 0 0 : x = 0 + 1 : x > 0 Well, perhaps not exactly as expected. If you’re reading this in Chrome (and, presumably, other Chrome-based browsers), all the cells in the array are aligned left, which puts the zero in the wrong spot, not vertically aligned with the ones. But that’s Chrome’s fault, not Pandoc’s. Since Pandoc understands the \begin{array} command, it can do matrices, too: k = E A L [ 1 − 1 − 1 1 ] So far, I’ve found only one small bug in Pandoc’s conversion from LaTeX to MathML. Here’s a simple formula that includes both a summation and a limit: $$ e^x = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{x^n}{n!} = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left( 1+ \frac{x}{n} \right)^n $$ This is what it should look like, a screenshot of the equation as rendered by LaTeX itself: But here’s how it comes out after passing the equation to Pandoc: e x = ∑ n = 0 ∞ x n n ! = lim ⁡ n → ∞ ( 1 + x n ) n The summation is fine, but the limit is formatted incorrectly. The n → ∞ part should be under the lim , not off to the side like a subscript. That subscript-like formatting is what you’d use for an inline equation, not a block equation. Let’s see what happened. Here’s the MathML produced by Pandoc: xml: 1: 2: 3: 4: ex 5: = 6: 7: ∑ 8: n=0 9: ∞ 10: 11: 12: xn 13: n! 14: 15: = 16: 17: lim⁡ 18: n→∞ 19: 20: 21: 22: ( 23: 1+ 24: xn 25: ) 26: 27: n 28: 29: 30: 31: e^x 32: = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{x^n}{n!} 33: = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left( 1+ \frac{x}{n} \right)^n 34: 35: 36: The problem with the rendering of the limit is in Line 17. There’s an empty ⁡ element after the lim element. That’s what’s messing up the formatting. If we remove that empty element, the limit gets formatted the way it should: e x = ∑ n = 0 ∞ x n n ! = lim n → ∞ ( 1 + x n ) n Obviously, I’m not going to try to fix Pandoc; I have no idea how to program in Haskell. data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 本文是Fernanda Eberstadt对1977年她在16岁时于安迪·沃霍尔工厂工作的一段回忆。她曾对安迪着迷，通过母亲的描述了解工厂内的故事。安迪在1968年被枪击后，性格发生变化。1976年，她终于通过父母介绍认识了安迪。首次见面在La Grenouille餐厅，安迪带 Bianca Jagger 出席，整个晚餐期间，Fernanda感到有些害羞和失望。安迪邀请她为《Interview》杂志撰稿，但她推荐的几位艺术家均被认为“太老”或“太古怪”。最终她提议编舞家Andy de Groat，安迪同意但认为《Einstein on the Beach》“臭不可闻”。Fernanda感到对话不如预期，但她对安迪的印象仍深刻。

43880560.article_content:
Burning Mao
Fernanda Eberstadt
T
he summer of 1977, when I was sixteen years old, I started work at Andy Warhol’s Factory.
I was a teen stalker, a fantasist who mostly preferred sitting on a stoop opposite someone’s house, noting the street-scene in my diary, to actually meeting the person inside, and Andy had long been one of my simmering obsessions.
My parents – New York society people with an interest in downtown art – had first met Andy in the late fifties, when my father was working as a fashion photographer and Andy was still an illustrator dressing windows for Bonwit Teller. My father liked to say that back then he’d thought Andy Warhol an embarrassing little creep whose determination to be famous was clearly doomed. But my mother had a taste for oddball dreamers and she and Andy became friends; she appeared in one of his 1964
Screen Tests
. I’d been raised on her stories of the Factory – the silver-tinfoil-walled spaceship where Andy, pedaling on his exercise bike, swigged codeine-infused cough syrup and watched his superstars squabble and self-destruct. Watched and subtly egged them on. At a certain point, my mother got spooked by how many of his beautiful, lost young creatures ended up dead.
In 1968, Andy was shot by Valerie Solanas and he too, briefly, died. It was a time when America’s chickens, in Malcolm X’s phrase, seemed to be coming home to roost – Andy’s shooting was edged off the front pages by Robert F. Kennedy’s two days later – and when Andy came back from the dead, with his insides shattered and sewn together again, he was seemingly cured of his taste for watching other people detonate.
O
n 7 December 1976, I finally succeeded in pestering my parents into introducing me to Andy Warhol.
By then, they had devolved into merely social, semi-professional friends who exchanged poinsettia plants at Christmas, and the Andy I had wanted to know – the ghostly cyclist who could mesmerize you for eight hours with a flickery image of a skyscraper – had been supplanted by the art-businessman flanked by pinstripe-suited managers. And I too was in a different phase. By the time I actually made it to the Factory, I was less interested in Andy than in dancing at Studio 54 with his managers.
O
ur first meeting was at La Grenouille, a fancy French restaurant in Midtown. My parents had invited Andy to dinner, and later that night, I wrote my first impression of him in my diary. Andy was ‘
standing there in his dinner jacket and blue jeans, tape recorder tucked under his arm, looking shy and uncertain but friendly
’. He had brought as his date Bianca Jagger, gorgeous in a purple fox stole and a gold lamé toque. They ordered oysters and a spinach soufflé, which she sent back because, as she explained to the waiter, it was
affreux
. ‘
Halfway through dinner Mummy asked me to switch places with her so I could talk to Andy. Andy said something about my mother being “mean” not to let me sit next to him before. So we talked the rest of the evening. I was a little shy and ended up feeling oddly depressed and dispirited, sort of drained. He said I looked like a movie star, had I ever thought of being one. That seemed like the sort of thing he says to about five hundred people a week . . . He asked me to bring down my whole class to the studio – that too I found depressing. I asked “Why don’t you come to Brearley
[the private girls’ school where I was in eleventh grade]
?” He said no, he could never do that, something about being too shy. I said, “Well, a lot of them are really awful.” He said, “Well, bring the awful ones too.” He’s very easy to talk to,
I kept saying things I wished I hadn’t.’
My mother had told Andy I was a writer and he asked if there was anyone I wanted to write about for his magazine
Interview
.
He said they needed something for the January issue.
‘“We want someone young and really new – what have you seen on Broadway, who can you think of” on and on, I was completely stuck. Ludicrously I suggested Mr
[Edward]
Gorey. Andy said, “Oh come on. He’s creepy – he’s really old. I saw him walking along Park Avenue the other day. He’s too peculiar for me.” That made me laugh. “Too peculiar for you? He’s just a bit moldy. I was obsessed with him for about two years.” Mr Gorey’s star was pretty dim that night.’
I suggested other writers, photographers, film-makers whose work I admired. All too old, too peculiar. Finally, I proposed the choreographer Andy de Groat, who had just collaborated on Philip Glass and Robert Wilson’s
Einstein on the Beach
.
Andy agreed, ‘
though he thought
Einstein on the Beach
was “stinky”. He wanted some more people. I told him I’d provide some later. Andy said to call A de G tomorrow, and then him. “The piece has to be in really soon.”
’
Andy’s description of the evening, published in his Diaries, accords with mine, but he added a nice coda. ‘

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： Warren Buffett退休及其影响的多角度讨论

不同观点：
• 对Buffett退休的感慨和尊敬：一些评论者对Buffett在94岁高龄仍能参与工作表示钦佩，认为这是一个时代的结束（riffraff, nu11ptr）。
• Buffett的激励作用：有评论提到Buffett的演讲和小谈话对他们的生活和健康习惯产生了积极影响（apexalpha）。
• Buffett的政治观点和经济政策：部分讨论集中在他对关税和富人税的看法，以及他与奥巴马政府的非正式合作（tchalla, andrewl）。
• 对Buffett投资成功的分析：有评论者对Buffett长期战胜市场的“秘密”感兴趣，并提出了他是否在市场外积累了财富的疑问（deeg）。
• Buffett对伯克希尔的影响：有人质疑90岁以上的人继续领导大型企业的有效性，并对伯克希尔在Buffett退休后的未来表示怀疑（aliljet）。

补充讨论：
• Buffett的遗产和影响力：有评论质疑Buffett对普通人生活的实际影响，认为他主要是为富人和投资者服务（khazhoux）。
• 对未被政府重用的遗憾：有评论者感到遗憾，认为像Buffett这样的人物未能在政府中担任重要的经济职位（ivape）。
• Berkshire股东大会的独特性：有评论者分享了参加伯克希尔股东大会的独特体验，将其比作资本主义的盛会（moomin）。
• 学术分析和资源推荐：有评论提供了关于Buffett投资策略的学术论文链接，供他人参考（Jhsto）。
• 关于Buffett生活方式的趣闻：有评论提到Buffett作为可口可乐的忠实消费者，每天饮用五罐可乐的趣闻（havaloc）。

争议焦点：
• Buffett的实际影响和贡献：部分评论者质疑Buffett对普通人和社会的影响是否如人们所认为的那样显著（khazhoux）。
• 高龄领导者是否应继续掌舵：对于高龄领导者继续管理大型企业是否合适存在不同看法（aliljet）。

data.author: nkurz

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于如何应对螺旋虫害的讨论，涉及不同方法和观点，以及对美国和墨西哥政府应对措施的评价。

不同观点：
• **支持通过昆虫不育技术（SIT）控制螺旋虫**：throwup238和accrual强调通过释放不育雄虫来消灭螺旋虫的有效性，并指出美国农业部（USDA）和动物植物健康检查局（APHIS）已经在进行相关工作。然而，throwup238提到墨西哥政府的官僚限制延误了该计划的执行。

• **质疑使用伊维菌素（ivermectin）**：neuroelectron提出使用伊维菌素来治疗宠物鼠的寄生虫问题，质疑其是否也可用于控制螺旋虫害。这一观点并未详细讨论其在大规模农业中的可行性。

• **对进口和肉类消费的批评**：reverendsteveii和unfitted2545从不同角度批评了对进口的依赖和肉类消费的现状。reverendsteveii主张严惩进口，而unfitted2545则借机提倡素食主义。

• **讽刺和幽默的观点**：davidw和labster以讽刺的口吻评论应对措施，davidw建议给牛喂胡萝卜汁、鱼肝油和姜黄，labster则提到依赖自由贸易政策进口牛肉。

• **对政府应对措施的失望**：Krasnol和andsoitis对政府应对螺旋虫害的措施表示失望，Krasnol将整个国家比作电影主题公园，暗示应对不力，andsoitis则担心螺旋虫害在美国复发带来的严重后果。

补充讨论：
• **对具体操作的关注**：danso对如何通过操作减少牛的压力表示好奇，并引用了一个关于牛粪影响利润的例子。

• **其他文化参考**：scandox提到通过阅读Alice Sheldon的小说《The Screwfly Solution》了解螺旋虫害，显示出文学作品在普及科学知识方面的作用。snowwrestler提供了一篇关于螺旋虫害屏障的详细报道，为讨论增添了背景信息。

争议焦点：
• **墨西哥政府的限制措施**：throwup238指出墨西哥政府对USDA和APHIS飞行和释放不育虫的限制是项目执行的主要障碍，这一问题在评论中引发了对跨国合作和官僚效率的讨论。

总的来说，讨论围绕螺旋虫害的控制方法、政府和国际合作的有效性以及肉类消费和进口政策展开，展现了多种视角和意见。

data.title: Ask HN: Anyone else roll eyes at startups that went from "X" to "AI-powered X"?
data.author: ronbenton
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI技术及AI标签在商业和营销中的使用及其影响

不同观点：
• **反对过度使用AI标签**：
   - [perrygeo] 认为很多公司只是简单地使用AI标签来提升自己的形象，实际上并没有真正开发AI技术。他批评那些只是将AI消费作为产品一部分的公司，并将其比作"用Rust重写X"这样的市场策略。
   - [shikon7] 和 [tacticalturtle] 提供了具体例子，说明一些公司通过改名来搭上AI的潮流，实际上并没有实质性变化。
   - [unkoman] 指出很多公司使用"AI增强"作为卖点，但实际上没有显著区别。
   - [manchmalscott] 表示对AI的过度宣传感到极度厌倦，任何提到AI的宣传都会让他失去兴趣。

• **支持AI作为重要技术趋势**：
   - [danenania] 认为AI可以提升大多数产品的实用性，尽管不是所有公司都能很好地实施AI技术，但忽视这一技术转变并不是明智的选择。
   - [dragonwriter] 指出AI目前主要作为向风投（VCs）销售公司的卖点，而不是直接向消费者销售产品的卖点，这种品牌营销反映了初创公司的融资需求。

• **对AI标签商业化的批评与理解**：
   - [rvz] 批评一些公司为了获得风投资金而将自己标榜为"AI公司"，实际上只是调用他人的AI模型，并指出这种现象类似于以前公司称自己为"互联网公司"或"机器人公司"。
   - [nikanj] 认为即使对AI标签感到不屑，但将其加入宣传材料确实能够吸引投资，因为当前投资者对非AI项目缺乏兴趣。

补充讨论：
• **AI标签的市场效应**：
   - [sejje] 表示对各种营销手段持怀疑态度，但承认这些手段可能有效。
   - [Arubis] 认为自己不是AI标签的目标受众，因为其技术背景和对资本市场的不同关注点。
   - [DoctorOW] 将AI标签的营销策略比作曾经的热门趋势（如VR），指出这是一种获取资金的常见策略。

争议焦点：
• AI标签是否被滥用以及是否对公司和投资者有实质意义。一方认为这是市场炒作，另一方则认为AI作为技术趋势不容忽视。

data.title: Psilocybin reduced depression symptoms as much as leading antidepressant (2021)
data.author: dp-hackernews
data.article_summary: 一项发表于《新英格兰医学杂志》的研究比较了裸盖菇素与SSRI类药物艾司西酞普兰对重度抑郁症的疗效。该研究由伦敦帝国理工学院迷幻研究中心进行，为期六周，参与者为59名中重度抑郁症患者。研究通过16项抑郁症状快速量表（QIDS-SR-16）评估，发现两者均能减轻抑郁症状，且无显著差异。然而，其他次要指标显示，裸盖菇素可能比艾司西酞普兰更有效。尽管研究规模较小，且存在志愿者非随机 enrollment和盲法可能被破译的局限性，但该研究为未来探索裸盖菇素的治疗潜力提供了重要参考。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

43880979.article_content:
Photo by
Önder Örtel
on
Unsplash
Since their introduction
in the late 1980s
, selective-serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) have become the
go-to
treatment for major depression. SSRIs, however, have a number of limitations: they take
several weeks
to start working, can cause a variety of
side-effects
, and
do not help
some people with depression. A series of recent
clinical investigations
suggest that psilocybin, the active compound in magic mushrooms, may be an effective alternative. One question that these studies left unanswered, however, is how effective psilocybin treatment is compared to SSRIs.
In a first-of-its-kind
study
recently published in
The New England Journal of Medicine
, researchers at the
Center for Psychedelic Research at Imperial College London
compared psilocybin and escitalopram, an SSRI drug sold under the name Lexapro, as treatments for major depression. The six-week long study enrolled 59 volunteers with moderate-to-severe major depression. They were randomly and blindly assigned to receive treatment with psilocybin and an escitalopram control, or escitalopram and a psilocybin control. All the participants also received psychological support.
Psilocybin and escitalopram both reduce depression symptoms
To evaluate the two treatments, the researchers compared the change from baseline on the
16-item Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology–Self-Report
(QIDS-SR-16), a basic clinical measure of depression symptoms. Based on results of the QIDS-SR-16, psilocybin and escitalopram both reduce depression symptoms. The researchers did not detect a statistically significant difference between the two treatments.
The results of other measures taken in the study, however, suggest that psilocybin may be more effective than escitalopram. When designing the study, the researchers determined that the QIDS-SR-16 most directly addressed their experimental question and would therefore be the primary outcome measure, but they also evaluated depression symptoms with a number of additional scales. Nearly all secondary outcome measures favored psilocybin over escitalopram, but their results hold less weight than the QIDS-SR-16 because of how the study was designed.
The study
was also limited
by its small size, non-random enrollment of interested volunteers, and the possibility that participants may have been unblinded by the strong subjective effects of psilocybin or the well-known side-effects of SSRIs. Nonetheless, as the most rigorous evaluation of the therapeutic potential of psilocybin conducted to date, the results provide a benchmark for the design of future investigations.

data.title: Redis is open source again
data.author: antirez
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Redis 许可证变更及其对社区和用户的影响

不同观点：
• [c0l0] 认为 Redis 公司的许可证变更（从自由开源软件 FOSS 变更为 SSPL）让他们感到背叛，尽管他们对 AGPL 没有道德上的反对。他们不再信任 Redis 公司，并决定转向使用 Redis 的分支（如 Valkey）。
• [simonw] 对 Redis 重新转回开源许可证表示欢迎，认为这是一个明智的决定，并希望其他公司也能效仿。他提到 Redis 的新功能（如 Redis Query Engine）使其更具吸引力，并强调社区希望看到这样的变化。
• [placatedmayhem] 质疑社区是否会重新信任 Redis 公司，并指出一些大公司的法律部门对 AGPL 许可证持谨慎态度，这可能使 Valkey 等更具吸引力的选择。
• [kamranjon] 强调 Redis 的技术优势和 API 设计的简洁性，认为 Redis 一直在推动技术进步，并让用户能够探索新技术。他表示对 Redis 的未来充满信心。
• [aftbit] 质疑 Redis 公司的目标是否真的是为了社区利益，认为强迫大用户维护自己的分支并不利于任何人。同时，他指出，既然有大公司维护的 Valkey，为什么还要使用 Redis？
• [md3911027514] 表示他们的公司已经转向 Valkey，并投入了大量工程时间，不打算再转回 Redis，因为担心 Redis 会再次变更许可证。
• [rustc] 指出 Redis 仍然要求贡献者签署贡献者许可协议（CLA），这意味着他们有可能再次变更许可证，只有接受 AGPL 许可证的补丁才能确保开源永久性。
• [theturtletalks] 引用 Antirez 的博客文章，强调他对代码的艺术性追求，并对他重新参与 Redis 项目表示欣慰。
• [bradgessler] 提到曾收到 Redis 公司关于商标使用的奇怪邮件，认为这是他们对技术社区态度傲慢的表现，并表示不再使用 Redis。
• [otterley] 认为许可证变更是一个单向门，一旦失去信任，很难再恢复。Redis 通过变更许可证失去了社区的信任。
• [remram] 表示不认为 Redis 的变更解决了问题，认为 Redis Labs 对社区造成了伤害，并表示更愿意使用 Valkey。
• [redbell] 提到 Redis 重新转回开源许可证是预料之中的，并感谢 Redis 团队的努力。
• [DetroitThrow] 认为虽然信任的恢复需要时间，但转回 AGPL 是一个好的开始，希望这能鼓励更多公司选择开源许可证。

补充讨论：
• Redis 公司要求签署 CLA 的问题引发了对未来再次变更许可证的担忧。
• Redis 的新功能（如 Redis Query Engine）被认为是吸引用户回归的重要因素。
• 大公司对 AGPL 许可证的谨慎态度可能使 Valkey 等分支更具吸引力。
• 社区对 Redis 公司的信任问题是一个重要的讨论点，许多人表示不再信任 Redis 公司。
• Antirez 的回归和他对代码艺术性的追求被一些用户视为 Redis 项目的重要价值。

• Redis 的新功能（如 Redis Query Engine）被认为是吸引用户回归的重要因素。
• 大公司对 AGPL 许可证的谨慎态度可能使 Valkey 等分支更具吸引力。
• 社区对 Redis 公司的信任问题是一个重要的讨论点，许多人表示不再信任 Redis 公司。
• Antirez 的回归和他对代码艺术性的追求被一些用户视为 Redis 项目的重要价值。

data.title: Spain-Portugal blackouts: what happened
data.author: VagabundoP
data.article_summary: 2025年4月28日，西班牙半岛电力系统在上午一切正常，需求与发电量匹配。然而，在12:30至12:35之间，电网出现异常，导致全伊比利亚半岛大停电。此前，可再生能源，尤其是光伏太阳能，满足了大部分电力需求。然而，风电出力突然飙升，法国停止从西班牙进口电力，导致供需失衡。与此同时，核电站因过载自动关闭，光伏发电量也从18,000 MW骤降至8,000 MW。尽管最初怀疑是网络攻击，最终认为可能是技术故障。此次事件凸显了电网管理和可再生能源整合的挑战，对伊比利亚及欧洲有重要借鉴意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：可再生能源与电网稳定性问题，以及相关政策和技术解决方案

不同观点：

• throw09093：指出负电价导致太阳能自动断开连接，以及核能由于过载也断开连接，认为这是一个会计软件的bug，可能大量太阳能电厂使用相同的软件，导致问题扩大。
• agarsev：提到异常的天气情况（持续降雨导致水库满溢）可能与停电有关，质疑这是否是停电的原因之一。
• timmg：对可再生能源缺乏大规模储能系统表示担忧，质疑当前是否有实用的储能系统可以支持可再生能源成为主要电力来源。

• 文章中关于太阳能无法自动响应频率变化的描述引发争议（johnea、Calwestjobs）。

• 对The Conversation/Europe新闻来源的信任和偏见问题（hyperman1）。
• 异常天气情况对电网和能源系统的潜在影响（agarsev）。
• 对大规模储能系统可行性和成本的讨论（timmg、briandw）。
• 具体技术解决方案的可行性，如光伏阵列提供“惯性”的建议（jmole）。

On the morning of Monday 28 April, nothing was out of the ordinary in peninsular Spain’s electricity system. Demand was at normal levels for the time of year, and was being easily met by the total generation capacity available.
The day before, the Spanish National Grid Network (REE,
Red Eléctrica Española
, commercially known as Redeia) had held its
usual daily auction
to determine which facilities would supply energy over the course of the following day. REE manages electricity distribution in Spain, and though formally a private company it is controlled by the Spanish State, which owns 20% of its capital. Its
website
states that:
“We are responsible for ensuring that electricity is always available wherever you need it and for making it sustainable by promoting renewable energies. For all these reasons, Red Eléctrica is the backbone of the electricity system in Spain and the cornerstone of the ecological transition process that the country is undergoing.”.
Electric energy in peninsular Spain: demand vs forecast on 25 April 2025.
REE
12:30: business as usual
At 12:30, most of the country’s energy demand was being covered by renewable sources, especially photovoltaic solar energy, which was contributing just over half of the total. This situation had been repeated throughout the month, as in Spain the combined capacity of solar and wind energy can, given the right conditions, cover the country’s entire electricity demand during the brightest hours in the middle of the day.
The country’s nuclear plants, as planned, were operating at half their usual capacity because, according to their owners, the high charges they are subject to make them economically unviable during periods when the price of electricity is very low.
At that time the price of electricity on the official market was
in the negative
at around -1€/MWh. At these prices Spain was exporting electricity to Morocco, Portugal, and even France. In addition, much of the available energy was being used to pump water from low lying river basins into reservoirs – the only practical way to store energy on a large scale. However, this capacity has a limit and, with the reservoirs almost full, it cannot continue to be stored indefinitely.
Electric Energy Spain Peninsular generation at 12:30 on 28 April 2025.
REE
12:33: something strange happens
In the five minutes between 12:30 and 12:35, something anomalous happened which is still yet to receive an official explanation: a
sudden drop in the Iberian electricity grid
causes a total blackout.
For the first few minutes confusion reigned, aggravated by the disruption of landline and mobile phone networks. Rumours circulated that other European countries were affected (I myself heard this on the battery-powered radio that I had rushed out to buy), and fingers were quickly pointed at a possible cyber-attack. I doubted this hypothesis, as the computer networks that control electrical systems are usually disconnected from the internet, and a Europe-wide grid outage would lead to something closely resembling an episode of Black Mirror.
After a few minutes my radio, my lifeline, announced that the blackout was limited to the Iberian peninsula, meaning the most likely cause was a technical failure.
What went wrong?
When analysing the available data available from REE between 12:30 and 12:35, we can observe several unusual events.
A few minutes before the outage, fluctuations were observed in the grid, and there was a spike in wind power generation, which had been very low until then. France suddenly stopped importing electricity from Spain, perhaps because it detected a problem in the peninsular grid, and this deepened the imbalance between supply and demand.
At that point, the few operating nuclear power plants received an overload signal. In accordance with protocol, control rods were inserted and they were automatically shut down.
But what was most surprising was the behaviour of solar photovoltaics, which dropped sharply from generating 18,000 MW to just 8,000 MW in just a few seconds. Since the sun had not vanished, it must have been an automated command that switched off thousands of solar facilities.
REE sou

data.title: How much I have(n't) made angel investing
data.author: alexcos
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：天使投资的策略及其潜在回报

不同观点：
• slouischarles认为，一些顶级的天使投资人往往处于创业创始人网络中。他提出一个假设，即如果有人只对有过两次或以上创业经历的创始人进行天使投资，是否会有不同的回报。这个观点的核心是关注创始人的经验对投资回报的影响，暗示多次创业的创始人可能具备更高的成功率，从而为投资人带来更好的回报。

• k-i-r-t-h-i则从另一个角度提出，标普500指数（SPY）自2012年以来上涨了约4倍，建议人们考虑更被动的投资策略，尤其是在选股方面。他的观点强调了被动投资的潜在收益，暗示主动挑选创业公司进行天使投资可能并非最佳选择，尤其是在市场整体表现良好的情况下。

补充讨论：
• slouischarles的评论引发了对创始人经验与投资回报之间关系的思考，强调了特定投资策略（专注于多次创业者）的可能性。
• k-i-r-t-h-i的评论则提醒投资者关注更广泛的市场趋势，暗示在某些情况下，被动投资可能比主动挑选个别股票或创业公司更为稳妥和有利。

争议焦点：
• 两种观点的核心争议在于主动投资（如天使投资特定类型的创始人）与被动投资（如跟随市场指数）的优劣。具体来说，slouischarles关注的是通过特定策略主动挑选投资对象的潜在优势，而k-i-r-t-h-i则强调了被动投资在长期内的稳定收益。这反映了投资策略选择中的一个经典争论：主动管理与被动管理的相对优劣。

data.article_summary: Anukari是一款基于3D物理模拟的软件合成器与效果处理器。用户可以通过拖放质量块、弹簧等物理组件，设计自己的3D乐器或效果，并实时看到和听到结果。它支持MIDI和MPE控制器，允许创建复杂的物理系统并进行高度自定义的调制。Anukari利用GPU处理音频，支持插件和独立运行，适合Windows和MacOS系统。它还提供实时3D界面和定制视觉效果，可以创造独特的混响、故障音效等。目前处于Beta阶段，以50%折扣价销售。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对一款基于物理建模的音频合成工具的评论，涉及产品定位、功能建议、技术讨论和用户体验等方面。

不同观点：
• Deng（程序员/物理学家 vs 音乐家身份的冲突）：作为程序员和物理学家对该工具有很大兴趣，但作为音乐家则担心操作复杂性与产出是否成正比。认为目前展示的音色例子不够吸引人，建议增加更复杂的音色演示和预设展示，以吸引音乐家群体。
• AaronAPU：建议在页面顶部添加即时的音频视觉演示，减少用户获取音色和功能信息的阻力。
• Tarentel：虽然认为工具操作复杂且可能不会使用，但赞赏无需邮件即可下载试用的做法，并建议增加主音量控制功能。
• 1R053：建议增加始终在调/音乐模式的功能，并提出类似NI插件的多键盘区域概念，以增强实用性。

补充讨论：
• Nayuki：提到音乐驱动3D动画的逆向概念，分享了Animusic的例子。
• Sitkack：希望看到与Audiocube（3D空间DAW）开发者的讨论，提供了相关链接。
• Sunray2：支持该项目，并表示希望贡献力量（作为白天的物理学家）。同时提到Korg柏林分部的Phase8乐器，认为该项目有艺术与生活相互模仿的意味。
• Ssfrr：对GPU音频处理的技术细节提出问题，关注最坏情况下的延迟和不同GPU类型之间的差异。
• Florilegiumson：赞赏GPU应用于声音合成，并对基于数值声音合成的数学原理提出思考。
• Adzm：纠正对Mick Gordon（DOOM原声带作者）的误称。
• Gitroom：尽管不擅长弹奏键盘，但仍被工具吸引。
• Imhoguy：认为该工具潜力无限，可以模拟真实乐器，并赞赏永久许可模式。
• Modeless：喜欢基于物理的音频工具，并分享了AngeTheGreat的引擎声音模拟视频作为参考。
• Michaelhoney：赞赏项目实现，表达对项目完成的钦佩。

争议焦点：
• Deng对于工具是否能吸引音乐家的质疑与其他用户（如Gitroom）对工具的纯粹赞赏形成对比，显示出用户群体对工具复杂性与实用性的不同期望。

技术讨论：

Anukari
3D Physics Synthesizer
Anukari is a software synthesizer and effects processor based on a fully interactive 3D physics simulation. Drag and drop physics components like masses and springs to design your own 3D instrument or effect. See and hear what you've built in real time.
Anukari is now in Beta. For the adventurous only: available to purchase for
50%
off.
$
70
$
140
Buy Now
Download free demo
Radically New MIDI Instrument
Use Anukari's 3D physics playground to create instruments you've only been able to imagine until now. Create a 3D instrument made from masses and springs, and then use your MIDI keyboard to trigger mallets, plectrums, bows, and traditional oscillators. Hook up virtual microphones to pick up the sound the 3D instrument makes. You can keep it simple, or build sprawling systems of hundreds of masses.
Powerful Effects Processor
Anukari can accept audio input signals, either as a sidechain input alongside MIDI or as the primary input. Create 3D audio signal inputs and connect them to the parts of the physics system you want to vibrate, and then pick up the resulting sounds with virtual microphones. Throw in a couple dozen delay lines for reverb or feedback effects. And heck, why not use some LFOs to modulate the spring stiffness? Whatever you can dream up, you can build.
Full MPE Support
Works with both "legacy" MIDI and Midi Polyphonic Expression (MPE), so you can use a regular MIDI keyboard or your Linnstrument, Roli Seaboard, Haken Continuum, or other favorite MPE controller with Anukari. All MPE inputs can be custom-mapped to modulate arbitrary physics parameters, or left alone with their satisfying defaults so you can just play.
Modulate All the Things
In addition to the basic physics objects, there are a ton of options for modulation. Powerful sample-accurate LFOs which can operate all the way up to audio frequency for FM. MIDI-triggered envelopes. Envelope followers. And of course, every MIDI control source, as well as DAW automation parameters. The modulation matrix is simple to understand: it's displayed via physical connections in the 3D world. And nearly every parameter can be modulated.
Unleash the Power of Your GPU
Anukari processes audio on your graphics card (GPU), so massive compute power is available to you, leaving your CPU power available for other plugins. Want to hear what 500 detuned oscillators on a single voice sounds like? Go ahead. Need a couple hundred LFOs for some crazy experimental glitch instrument? No problem. Create hundreds of plectrums. Because you can. What other reason could you possibly need?
Plugin and Standalone Mode
You can run Anukari in your favorite DAW on Windows or MacOS as a VST3, AU, or AAX plugin, or run it in standalone mode to play it as a MIDI instrument without the complexity of a DAW. Anukari only uses a fraction of your GPU's resources, so you can easily run multiple instances of the plugin in your DAW, perhaps using it both as a synthesizer and as an effects processor. The possibilities are endless.
Tactile Real-Time 3D Interface
Anukari isn't just another stylized faceplate covered in knobs. You create the instrument's physics layout in an intuitive 3D editor (kind of like a video game), and then see how it vibrates, flexes, spins, and moves in real-time as you play it. Drag and release a mass with the mouse to hear what it does! Or project fully-customizable 3D visuals during a show so the audience can see the 3D instrument that they're listening to while you play it.
Unbelievable Reverbs
Run external audio sources through any shape of spring system you can think of. Tune the parameters to get dark industrial caverns or crashing plates. Modulate the physics parameters with an LFO to get swirling reverb, and add delay lines for slapback or feedback effects. Or push up the gain until the 3D system is bent way out of shape and distorts in unexpected ways.
Bizarre Glitches and SFX
With a full 3D physics simulation, you can build some pretty weird stuff. Try a loose chain of masses tied down only at one end, struck by three mallets in different directions, and watch it spin wildly out of control. Push the physics past their limits and see how things explode. Create a loose tangled mass of springs and excite it with white noise. What will happen? Who knows. Find out!
Custom 3D Visuals
Anukari ships with a wide variety of built-in skyboxes, 3D models, and visual effect options, so you can fine tune the 3D look. Get the vibe right for the sounds you're making, or even project the live visuals for a show.
In addition to the built-in skyboxes and skins, Anukari has support for loading fully custom skyboxes and 3D models. Using 3D modeling software like Blender, advanced users can completely replace the 3D visuals, including the animations.
Featured on Sonic TALK
The original Anukari introduction video was featured on the Sonic TALK podcast hosted by Nick Batt, with guests Yoad Nevo, Paulee Bow, and Robin Vincent. Watch their discussion

data.title: The language brain matters more for programming than the math brain? (2020)
data.author: smusamashah
data.article_summary: 一项由华盛顿大学研究人员发表的研究表明，学习编程更依赖于语言能力和解决问题能力，而非数学能力。研究招募了42名参与者，通过Codeacademy完成Python课程，并进行数学技能、工作记忆、问题解决能力和第二语言学习能力的预测试。研究发现，学习Python的速度主要与语言能力和一般认知能力（如问题解决和工作记忆）相关，而数学能力仅解释了2%的学习速度差异。脑电图（EEG）数据还显示，休息状态下的β振荡与语言学习能力相关，这也与编程学习速度有关。该研究挑战了编程需要强大数学能力的传统观点，表明语言技能在编程学习中起关键作用，尤其对那些自认不擅长数学的人来说是个鼓舞人心的发现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程学习中语言能力与数学能力的相对重要性，以及一项研究的方法论和结论的有效性。

不同观点：
• [john-h-k] 认为该研究的头条具有夸大性，研究结果不够严谨。他指出研究样本量小（仅36人），模型中的R^2值较低，且逐步回归分析存在问题。他认为研究中的“语言学习比数值能力更重要”的结论在统计上并不显著（p-value为0.772），且研究未能处理数据中的噪音问题。

• [albertoCaroM] 认为需要仔细阅读Prat等人（2020）的研究，指出研究中测量的数值能力与编程中所需的高级数学技能不同。他还强调Python作为一种易读的语言，可能对语言能力强的人有利，但不能推广到其他编程语言。此外，他认为语言和数学在认知基础上存在交互和互补，而非对立。

• [armchairhacker] 认为编程中的问题解决部分需要数学技能，而组织部分需要写作技能。他认为良好的代码不仅要解决问题，还要具备可读性和模块化，而写作技能对此有帮助。

• [QuercusMax] 以个人经历支持语言能力在编程中的重要性，提到自己优秀的阅读能力在编程生涯中非常有帮助。

• [jll29] 否定“语言脑”和“数学脑”的二分法，认为数学本身是一种人类创造的形式语言，与语言有着共同的认知基础。

• [godelski] 认为没有“语言脑”和“数学脑”的区分，且大多数人对数学的理解有限。他强调数学的本质是模式和抽象思维，而非单纯的计算。

• [sota_pop] 也认为“语言脑”和“数学脑”的区分是错误的二分法，并批评研究带有轻微的优生学倾向。他强调数学是一种语言，任何人都可以通过兴趣和努力成为优秀的程序员或数学家。

• [jboggan] 发现擅长英语拼字游戏的人往往也擅长学习编程，认为这与记忆和处理规则例外有关。

• [janalsncm] 对研究标题将问题解决技能与语言能力混为一谈表示怀疑，并指出研究中的“数学”实际上是“数值能力”，且研究已有五年历史。

• [dmos62] 认为编程与写作技能和工作记忆有关，并分享了自己因工作记忆不佳而发展出的编程风格。

• [Shorel] 定义数学为能够写出形式证明的能力，并认为编程中的算法涉及证明，因此也是数学。

• [canjobear] 以个人经历支持语言能力对学习编程的重要性，提到自己从语言学习中获得的技能帮助了Python的学习，并进一步引发了对数学的兴趣。

• [msvana] 指出研究原文提到了问题解决和语言能力，而文章标题仅关注语言能力是误导性的。此外，他认为数值能力只是数学技能的一小部分。

• [resters] 认为早期掌握编程语法的人往往擅长学习新的符号系统，但这可能是因为他们大脑中存在一种持久的类型I错误。而最终成为优秀程序员的人往往对语义和信息流有更深的理解。

• [tmaly] 对研究的小样本量（仅36人完成）表示怀疑，认为这影响了研究结果的可信度。

补充讨论：
- 研究的方法论问题，尤其是样本量小和逐步回归分析的局限性，是多个评论者关注的焦点。
- 多位评论者提到Python作为一种易读的语言可能对语言能力强的人有利，但不能推广到其他编程语言。
- 数学和语言在编程中的交互和互补关系也被多次提及，强调不应将二者对立起来。
- 个人经历和自我反思为多个评论提供了支持，显示了语言和数学能力在不同编程背景下的多样化影响。

Your language brain matters more for learning programming than your math brain
New research contradicts long held assumptions about coding
Amy R Nippert
Neuroscience
University of Minnesota
May 12, 2020
Comment
2 peer comments
Facebook
Share
Twitter
Tweet

Instapaper
Ad
When you think of learning another language, you probably think of French, Spanish, or Chinese. But what about Python or Java? The two processes might be more similar than you'd think.
A recent
study
published from researchers at the University of Washington showed that language ability and problem solving skills best predict how quickly people learn Python, a popular programming language. Their research, published in
Scientific Reports
, used behavioral tests and measures of brain activity to see how they correlated with how fast and well participants learned programming.
For the study, 42 participants were recruited to try a popular online coding course through
Codeacademy
. They were asked to complete ten 45-minute lessons of the "Learn Python" course. From the 36 participants who completed the study, they were able to determine rate of learning and how well the students learned the lessons.
Before doing online classes, participants did a battery of tests designed to look at math skills, working memory, problem solving, and second language learning ability. During their online programming course, the researchers were able to track how quickly they learned and how well they did in the quizzes built into the online software. They also completed a quiz and coding task at the end of the study to look at their overall coding knowledge.
How much did memory, problem solving, and an aptitude for numbers or languages influence how quickly they learned to code?
The researchers where then able to compare the test results from before and after the Python course. The goal was to determine how much of the differences in participant Python learning could be explained by their performance on the different pre-tests: how much did memory, problem solving, and an aptitude for numbers or languages influence how quickly they learned to code?
The participants learned Python at different rates, and had different programming abilities at the end of the study. The researchers looked at the relationship between the skills covered in the pre-test skills and the variability in how participants learned Python. They found that how
well
students learned Python was mostly explained by general cognitive abilities (problem solving and working memory), while how
quickly
they learned was explained by both general cognitive skills and language aptitude.
There's a lot of people out there who "aren't math people," but they just might be computer science people
Language aptitude explained almost 20% of the difference in how quickly people learned Python. In contrast, performance on the math pre-test only explained 2% of the variability in how quickly students learned, and didn't correlate at all with how well they learned. Learning to code depended much more on language skills than it did on numerical skills.
Python really is another language.
Wikimedia Commons
.
Additional evidence for the importance of language skills came from electroencephalography (EEG) data. EEG is a method of measuring brain activity through electrical patterns that can be recorded through the skull. Prior to their online learning tasks, participants were given a resting state EEG, which measures patterns in the brain when the subjects were relaxed and doing nothing.
Electrical activity at rest has different patterns. One of these patterns is slow waves of electrical activity called beta oscillations. Past research has shown that high levels of beta oscillations at rest are linked with the ability to learn a second
language
.
ulrcichw on
Pixabay
In this study, high levels of these beta oscillations were associated with faster learning and more programming knowledge. While this finding gives additional support to the connection between language learning and learning to code, it's not clear (yet) how beta oscillations are related to learning outcomes, and more research is needed.
Taken together, these result make the case for language skills being an integral aspect of learning programming (or at least of learning Python), while math skills weren't very predictive of how well or quickly participants learned. This idea has important implications for the perceptions surrounding programming, which is often viewed as a "math intensive" field.
Since language abilities were shown to predict ability to learn programming, perhaps women should have more of  a reputation for being "good" at programming.
There are many assumptions about programmers, especially about
who
makes a good programmer. Women often feel they don't fit with the idea of a "typical" computer
programmer
. However, girls typically have
higher
language skill

data.title: Both novelty and familiarity affect memory
data.author: amichail
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了新奇性和熟悉性对记忆的影响，以及如何利用这些原理来提高备考效率。研究表明，接触新奇环境可以激发大脑准备学习，从而更容易记住新信息。例如，在探索一个新环境后记忆单词的效果更好。另一方面，熟悉性帮助大脑将新信息归类到已有知识结构中，使其更容易被记住。利用已有的知识来理解新概念，可以增强记忆的整合和检索能力。例如，用香蕉和盐来形象化地记忆与神经传导相关的离子，这种视觉辅助工具能有效帮助学生理解抽象概念。因此，备考时可以通过接触新环境来激发学习状态，并利用已有知识来加深记忆。

When getting ready to take exams, it can sometimes feel as though there’s no way all the information you need to remember is going to fit in your brain. But there are ways to create the right conditions to make your studying as efficient as possible.
My research into the science of memory shows that both novelty – new experiences – and familiarity can affect memory. You can use novelty to prime yourself for learning, and familiarity to organise your memory and retain knowledge.
To start with, this might mean going for a walk in an unfamiliar part of your neighbourhood or looking at some art for the first time – in person or online – before you even start studying.
In the lab
, colleagues and I
have observed
that chances are higher that you will remember new information if you just visited an unfamiliar place.
In a typical experimental set-up, participants came to the lab to familiarise themselves with a virtual environment on a PC or with a virtual reality headset. This consisted of a fantasy island with unexpected elements, such as streetlight-sized candy canes. We invited our research participants to come back on two other occasions. During these sessions, they explored the same – now familiar – virtual environment, and one they hadn’t seen before.
After each round of virtual exploration, the experiment participants were presented with a series of words to try to commit to memory, which we then tested them on after a completely different “distractor” task that consisted of solving simple maths problems. Interestingly, the participants who had explored a new environment typically remembered more words than those who had explored a familiar one. This suggests that novelty may prepare the brain for learning.
After you’ve prepared your brain with a foray into the unknown, it’s time to harness familiarity.
Why the familiar is important
Learning entirely new information is often very challenging. Students sometimes report reading several pages, but having no recollection of what they read.
There may be several reasons for this, but a common one is that it is difficult to memorise something if it is very different from anything you have learned before.
The brain likes to categorise and label information, and our memory is organised in semantic categories. For example, if I mention “swivel chair”, “computer”, and “filing cabinet”, the overarching term “office” may pop to mind.
Memory associations like these are crucial during memory retrieval, as linked information can work as a memory cue. In memory research we sometimes refer to these interlinked concepts as
“memory schema”
.
When you have to learn something new, your brain will try to categorise that novel information. If a link can be made with something you already know, this information can more easily be integrated into an existing memory schema.
Based
on research
, we would predict that studying for a test is
more effective
if you already know something about the topic, as it allows you to put novel information in your existing memory schema, and allows you to retrieve that information more easily at a later point in time.
For example, imagine eating a yellow kiwi for the first time. Your previous experience with green kiwis will allow you to recognise the fruit. The novel experience of eating this slightly sweeter kiwi is easy to integrate in your existing knowledge of kiwis, including what they look, feel and taste like.
Making connections
But studying for exams often means learning abstract concepts. The related memory schemas are underdeveloped for less concrete information, which makes new information hard to remember.
In a biological psychology course I teach, students have to learn about the transfer of information between brain cells. One of the crucial aspects of this topic is the change in chemistry of the neuron, from when it is at rest to when it is firing, and the potassium and sodium chloride ions involved.
Exam results showed that students found these processes hard to remember. One year, I decided to introduce a simple visual memory aid: an image of a banana with a container of table salt on top.
Memory aid to help students remember ions involved in neural transmission.
Judith Schomaker

data.title: Bloom Filters
data.author: mfrw
data.article_summary: Bloom filters是一种由Burton Bloom在1970年提出的概率数据结构，旨在高效地进行集合成员检查，通过牺牲一定的准确性来大幅减少时间和空间消耗。其基本原理是使用一个位数组和多个哈希函数来记录元素的存在性。如果Bloom filter判断某个元素不在集合中，那么该判断是100%准确的；但如果判断元素在集合中，则可能存在假阳性。该结构特别适用于大多数查询结果为否的场景，能够显著加快系统速度并节省空间。通过设置不同的位数组大小和哈希函数数量，可以控制假阳性率。插入元素时，将其经过多个哈希函数计算，将结果位置的比特设为1；查询时，如果所有对应比特均为1，则可能存在（假阳性），如果有任何一个比特为0，则确定不存在。

43866001.article_content:
The original motivation for the creation of Bloom filters is efficient set
membership, using a probabilistic approach to significantly reduce the time and
space required to reject items that are not members in a certain set.
The data structure was proposed by Burton Bloom in
a 1970 paper
titled "Space/Time
Trade-offs in Hash Coding with Allowable Errors". It's a good paper that's
worth reading.
Why Bloom filters?
Suppose that we store some information on disk and want to check if a certain
file contains a certain entry. Reading from disk is time consuming, so we want
to minimize it as much as possible. A Bloom filter is a data structure that
implements a cache with probabilistic properties:
If the cache says the key is not present in a specific file, then it's
100% certain we should not be reading the file.
If the cache says the key
is
present in the file, there's a small chance
this is a false positive (and in fact the key isn't there). In this case
we just read the file as usual.
In a scenario where the majority of queries "is this key in that file?" have a
negative answer, a Bloom filter can significantly speed up the system
[1]
.
Moreover, the probabilistic nature (the existence of false positives) allows
Bloom filters to be extremely fast and occupy very little space. Here's a quote
from the Bloom paper:
The new hash-coding methods to be introduced are
suggested for applications in which the great majority of
messages to be tested will not belong to the given set. For
these applications, it is appropriate to consider as a unit of
time (called
reject time
) the average time required to
classify a test message as a nonmember of the given set.
How a Bloom filter works
A Bloom filter is a special kind of a
hash table with open addressing
.
It's an array of bits (the length is typically denoted
m
), and some fixed
number (
k
) of hash functions. We'll assume each hash function can take an
arbitrary sequence of bytes and hash it into an integer in the inclusive range
[0,
m-1]
. A Bloom filter supports two operations:
Insert an item
: the item is hashed using each of the
k
hash functions, and the
appropriate bits in the underlying array are set to 1.
Test if an item is a member
: the item is hashed using each of the
k
hash
functions. If any of the bits indicated by their results is 0, we return "false"
with certainty. If all the bits are 1, we return "true" - and there's a small
chance of false positives.
Here's how the Bloom paper describes it:
The hash area is considered as N individual addressable bits, with addresses 0
through N - 1. It is assumed that all bits in the hash area are first set to 0.
Next, each message in the set to be stored is hash coded into a number of
distinct bit addresses, say a1, a2, . . . , ad. Finally, all d bits addressed by
a1 through ad are set to 1.
To test a new message a sequence of d bit addresses,
say a'1, a'2, ... a'd, is generated in the same manner as for storing a message.
If all d bits are 1, the new message is accepted. If any of these bits is zero,
the message is rejected.
Hopefully it's clear why this data structure is probabilistic in nature: it's
possible that different items hash to the same number, and therefore when
we test some X, all its hashes point to bits turned on by the hashing of other
data. Read the Math appendix for the math behind Bloom filters and how to
calculate (and design for a specific) the false positive rate.
Here's an example:
We start with an empty bloom filter with
m=16
and
k=3
. All bits
are initialized to 0.
Insertion of "x". The three hashes return indices 1, 6, 15, so these bits
in the array are set to 1.
Insertion of "y". Hashing returns indices 6, 9 and 13, so these
bits in the array are set to 1. Note that bit 6 is set for both "x" and "y",
and that's fine.
Next, let's look at some membership tests:
Test "x". Hashing returns 1, 6, 15; all these bits are 1 in the
array, so the answer is "true". This is a true positive.
Test "w". Hashing returns 3, 9, 13. Since the bit at position 3 is 0, the
answer is "false".
Test "v". Hashing returns 9, 13, 15; all these bits are 1 in the array,
so the answer is "true". This is a false positive.
Note that it's trivial to prove (by the law of contraposition) that all "false"
answers from a Bloom filter's test operation are true negatives.
Implementation
Here's a simple implementation of a Bloom filter in Go:

// You can calculate m and k from the number of elements you expect the
// filter to hold and the desired error rate using CalculateParams.
func
New
(
m
uint64
,
k
uint64
)
*
BloomFilter
{
return
&
BloomFilter
{
m
:
m
,
k
:
k
,
bitset
:
newBitset
(
m
),
seed1
:
maphash
.
MakeSeed
(),
seed2
:
maphash
.
MakeSeed
(),
}
}
type
BloomFilter
struct
{
m
uint64
k
uint64
bitset
[]
uint64
// seeds for the double hashing scheme.
seed1
,
seed2
maphash
.
Seed
}
// Insert a data item into the bloom filter.
func
(
bf
*
BloomFilter

data.title: Testing AI's GeoGuessr Genius
data.author: vortex_ape
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了人工智能在GeoGuessr游戏中的惊人表现，GeoGuessr是一款根据随机谷歌街景图片猜测位置的游戏。OpenAI的最新模型o3能在仅提供一张图片的情况下精准定位到具体地点，如Marina State Beach, Monterey, CA。尽管其解释涉及沙色、浪高、天气等因素，一些人怀疑其可能通过隐藏元数据或作弊手段获得答案。为验证其能力，作者设计了一个严格的提示协议，避免模型依赖用户信息或不当线索，强调仅根据图片像素和公共网络搜索进行推理。文章探讨了超智能AI是否能完成看似不可能的任务，并反思了人类对超级智能策略的理解局限，类比人类与黑猩猩的智力差距。
